@graph.name: How to Remove AirPods Pro Tips Safely
@graph.description: Safely remove your AirPods Pro ear tips without causing damage. Follow these simple steps to unroll, pinch, and detach the tips properly.

step.name: Hold the AirPod securely
step.text: Tightly hold the AirPod by its head to prevent it from slipping.

itemListElement.text: Hold the AirPod by its head.

step.name: Unroll or invert the ear tip
step.text: Gently unroll or invert the ear tip to loosen it from the connector.

itemListElement.text: Gently unroll or invert the ear tip.

step.name: Pinch the base of the tip
step.text: Pinch the base of the tip with two fingers, making sure not to pull from the side or use your nails.

itemListElement.text: Pinch the base of the ear tip with two fingers.
Avoid pulling from the side or using your nails.

step.name: Pull the tip straight off
step.text: Pull the ear tip straight off the stem using light pressure. AirPods Pro tips use a snap-on connector, so a small amount of force is normal.

itemListElement.text: Pull the tip straight off with light pressure.
A little force is normal because of the snap-on connector.

@graph.name: How to Install New AirPods Pro Tips Properly
@graph.description: Easily install new AirPods Pro ear tips for the best fit and comfort. Follow these steps to align, attach, and secure the tips correctly.

step.name: Align the ear tip connector
step.text: Line up the oval connector on the ear tip with the oval edge of the AirPod.

itemListElement.text: Line up the oval connector on the tip with the oval edge of the AirPod.

step.name: Attach the ear tip
step.text: Push the ear tip onto the AirPod until you hear or feel a click, indicating it’s securely attached.

itemListElement.text: Push the tip in until you hear or feel a click.

step.name: Repeat for the other AirPod
step.text: Install the tip on the second AirPod and double-check both tips for a snug fit.

itemListElement.text: Repeat the process on the other AirPod.
Ensure both tips are fitted snugly.

keyPoints.explanation: AirPods Pro ear tips are soft silicone attachments that ensure noise isolation and improved sound quality by creating a better seal inside your ears.

keyPoints.title: Importance of Using Correct Ear Tip Size
keyPoints.explanation: Choosing the right ear tip size enhances sound quality, noise cancellation, comfort, and fit for workouts or long wear.

keyPoints.title: Safe Removal and Installation of Ear Tips

keyPoints.title: How to Choose the Best Fit with Testing

keyPoints.title: Maintenance and Replacement Practices**

title.rendered: WhatsApp View Once: How to Send Disappearing Photos and Videos on iPhone or Android

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What It Is: The “View Once” feature lets you send photos and videos that disappear after being opened once.
  • How to Send: To send “View Once” media, simply tap the ‘1’ icon next to the caption bar before sending.
  • For the Recipient: The recipient can view the media only once. It expires in 14 days if left unopened.
  • Key Limitations: “View Once” media cannot be saved, forwarded, starred, or shared, and it will expire if unopened.
  • Security Warning: This feature does not prevent screenshots, so only send “View Once” media to trusted contacts.

We all have private photos or quick snapshots we want to share—without them lingering forever in someone else’s gallery. That’s exactly where WhatsApp’s View Once feature comes in handy. This privacy-focused tool lets you send photos and videos that disappear immediately after they’ve been viewed. Perfect for one-time content, it gives you more control over what you share and for how long.

In this guide, I’ll walk you through everything you need to know about using View Once on WhatsApp, from how it works to when you should (or shouldn’t) use it.

What is View Once on WhatsApp?

As the name suggests, WhatsApp’s View Once feature allows you to send media (photos or videos) that the recipient can view only once. After viewing, the content disappears from the chat and can’t be saved or forwarded.

Here’s what makes View Once special:

  • The photo or video can only be viewed once.
  • It won’t be saved to the recipient’s gallery or chat history.
  • You’ll see an “Opened” label once the recipient has viewed it.
  • The recipient can’t take screenshots or screen recordings—attempts will result in a “Screen Capture Blocked” message.

Why Use View Once on WhatsApp?

Still wondering if it’s worth using? Here are some benefits of sending View Once media:

  • Better privacy: The content disappears after viewing, reducing the risk of it being saved or misused.
  • Less clutter: Ideal for sending temporary media like one-time passwords, outfit checks, or food pics.
  • Prevents resharing: The recipient can’t forward, save, or star the media.
  • Works in group chats: It’s not just limited to one-on-one conversations.

How to Send View Once Photos or Videos on WhatsApp

Ready to try it out? Follow these steps to send disappearing media via WhatsApp:

  1. Open WhatsApp and choose the conversation (individual or group).
  2. Tap the plus (+) icon next to the message field, then tap the Photos button in the pop-up menu.
  3. Alternatively, you can tap the Camera button to capture and share a photo directly from the app.
  4. Select the photo or video you want to share, tap the circled 1 (View Once) icon in the message field, then hit the Send button as you normally would.

Once the recipient views the photo or video, it disappears permanently from the chat.

What Does the Recipient See?

When someone receives a View Once photo or video:

  • It appears as a blurred thumbnail with a “1” icon.
  • They won’t see a preview until they open it.
  • Once viewed, the media can’t be opened again.
  • WhatsApp will mark the message as “Opened” underneath.
  • They have 14 days to open it before it expires automatically.

Limitations of WhatsApp View Once

While this feature enhances privacy, it’s not without some limitations:

  • Media sent using View Once can’t be saved, forwarded, starred, or reshared.
  • If the recipient has read receipts turned off, you won’t know if they’ve viewed it.
  • If the media was backed up before viewing, it could be restored.
  • It disappears after 14 days if not opened.

So, while the tool is useful, don’t use it as a guarantee for complete secrecy.

Privacy and Security Tips When Using View Once Media

To stay on the safe side while using this feature:

  • Only share View Once content with people you trust.
  • Keep in mind that someone could still take a photo using another device.
  • Review group members before sharing in group chats.
  • Let your recipient know the media is time-sensitive and viewable only once.

View Once Media vs. Disappearing Messages

Though both are privacy tools, View Once and Disappearing Messages serve different purposes.

Fix: WhatsApp View Once Not Working?

If View Once isn’t working for you, try these quick solutions:

  • Update WhatsApp to the latest version.
  • Check availability in your region (some features roll out gradually).
  • Verify your internet connection and restart the app.
  • Ensure you tap the “View Once” icon before sending.

One-Time View, Long-Term Privacy

WhatsApp’s View Once feature is a smart way to share media more privately. While it’s a great tool, it’s always wise to share with caution. No feature is completely foolproof—but this one gets close.

Have any questions or tips to share? Let us know in the comments below!

  • Cool WhatsApp Tips and Tricks for iPhone
  • How to send photos as documents in WhatsApp on iPhone without losing quality
  • How to Use Two WhatsApp Accounts on iPhone

keyPoints.title: WhatsApp's View Once Feature
keyPoints.explanation: This feature allows users to send photos or videos that disappear immediately after being viewed, enhancing privacy and control over shared media.

keyPoints.title: How to Use View Once on WhatsApp
keyPoints.explanation: Users can activate View Once by selecting the media, tapping the 'View Once' icon, and sending it; the content then vanishes after the recipient views it.

keyPoints.title: Recipient's Experience with View Once
keyPoints.explanation: Recipients see a blurred thumbnail with a '1' icon, and once opened, the media can’t be viewed again, marked as 'Opened,' and expires after 14 days if unopened.

keyPoints.title: Limitations of View Once Media
keyPoints.explanation: Media sent with View Once cannot be saved, forwarded, or reshared, and may be backed up before viewing, but disappears after 14 days if not opened.

keyPoints.title: Tips for Secure Use of View Once Media
keyPoints.explanation: Share only with trusted contacts, be aware of potential screenshots, review group members, and clarify that media is time-sensitive and viewable only once.

title.rendered: How to Play Xbox Games on Your iPhone and iPad

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Cloud Gaming (No Console): Stream Xbox games to your iPhone with Game Pass Ultimate, no console required, via Xbox Cloud Gaming.
  • Remote Play (Your Console): With Xbox Remote Play, you can stream games directly from your own Xbox console to your iPhone.
  • The Key Difference: Cloud Gaming streams from Microsoft’s servers (subscription needed), while Remote Play streams from your personal Xbox console.
  • Game Libraries: Cloud Gaming has a curated library (some with touch), while Remote Play streams any game you have installed.
  • Optimize Your Experience: For the best experience, connect a Bluetooth controller and use a stable, fast 5GHz Wi-Fi network.

Imagine playing Halo, Forza, Fortnite, or FIFA right on your iPhone or iPad—no bulky console or TV, just your device and maybe a controller. Sounds wild? It’s been a reality for some time.

Whether you own an Xbox or not, Microsoft lets you stream Xbox games directly to your iOS device using Xbox Cloud Gaming or Remote Play. We’ll show you how so you can turn your iPhone into a pocket-sized Xbox.

Why Play Xbox Games on Your iPhone or iPad?

Playing Xbox games on your iPhone or iPad is a convenient way to play your favorite console games from virtually anywhere. Whether you’re traveling, don’t have access to your TV, or just want to game from bed, you can do just that with the right method.

How to Play Xbox Games on an iPhone and iPad

There are two ways to play Xbox games on an iPhone or iPad. You can do this using Xbox Cloud Gaming (no Xbox required) or Xbox Remote Play (Xbox console needed). Let’s go through both methods in detail.

Play Xbox Games on an iPhone and iPad Using Xbox Cloud Gaming (xCloud)

Xbox Cloud Gaming (also known as xCloud) is Microsoft’s game streaming service that lets you play Xbox games directly from the cloud on your iPhone or iPad—no console required. Since the games run on Microsoft’s servers, you can stream AAA Xbox titles on virtually any screen, including your iPhone. All you need is an Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscription, a stable internet connection, and a supported controller. Think of it as Netflix for games, but instead of watching, you’re actually playing in real time.

Here’s everything you need to get started with Xbox Cloud Gaming on your iPhone or iPad:

  • Xbox Game Pass Ultimate ($14.99/month)
  • iPhone XR or newer, iPad Air 3rd Gen or newer (iOS 14.4+)
  • Safari browser (Chrome and Edge also work, but Safari is recommended)
  • Bluetooth-enabled Xbox controller or supported third-party controller
  • 10 Mbps+ internet speed (20 Mbps recommended for tablets)
  • 5GHz Wi-Fi connection

Once you have everything ready, here’s how to launch and start playing Xbox games using Cloud Gaming on your iPhone or iPad:

  1. Open Safari and go to Xbox’s Cloud Gaming website.
  2. Sign in using your Microsoft account, which is tied to your Game Pass Ultimate.
  3. Tap the Share icon at the bottom of Safari.
  4. Select Add to Home Screen and tap Add.

  5. You should now see an icon for the Cloud Gaming website on your Home Screen. Tap it to open the website.
  6. Pair your controller via Bluetooth from the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.
  7. Tap on a game, and you’re ready to play.

Play Xbox Games on an iPhone and iPad Using Remote Play

Xbox Remote Play is a feature that allows you to stream games from your own Xbox console to your iPhone or iPad over the internet. Instead of playing on your TV, you can access your installed games remotely from another room or even another location entirely. Your Xbox acts as the game server, and your iPhone or iPad becomes the screen and controller input device. It’s a great option if you already have an Xbox and want to continue your gaming session while away from your console. Just remember, the console must remain powered on (or in Instant-on mode) and connected to the internet.

Before you can start using Remote Play, make sure you have the following essentials set up and ready to go:

  • Xbox One, Series S, or Series X
  • iPhone XR or newer with iOS 13+
  • Xbox app (download from App Store)
  • Xbox Wireless Controller or supported alternative
  • Same Microsoft account on both devices
  • Strong Wi-Fi connection (5GHz recommended)

Once your devices are ready, follow these steps to connect your Xbox console and iPhone or iPad so you can start streaming games remotely.

Read More: Every game announced at Xbox Games Showcase 2026

On your Xbox:

  1. Press the Xbox button and go to Profile & System > Settings.
  2. Go to Devices & Connections > Remote Features.

  3. Enable Remote Features and set Power Mode to Instant-On.

On your iPhone or iPad:

  1. Open the Xbox app and sign in with your Microsoft account.
  2. Tap My Library > Consoles.
  3. Select your console and tap Remote Play on This Device.

  4. Pair your controller via Bluetooth.
  5. Start playing any installed game.

What is the Difference Between Cloud Gaming and Remote Play?

Are you unsure which method is right for you? Here’s a side-by-side comparison that breaks down the key differences between Xbox Cloud Gaming and Xbox Remote Play so you can decide which one best suits your setup and play style.

Whether you’re a casual gamer or a hardcore Xbox fan, this setup brings a vast library of console games to your iPhone or iPad. If you don’t own an Xbox, Cloud Gaming instantly gives you a taste of premium titles. If you already have a console, Remote Play lets you continue your gaming from anywhere, even your bed or a boring train ride. As Xbox and Apple slowly get along, this might just be the beginning of portable console gaming.

What Xbox Games are Compatible With iPhone and iPad?

You can play any cloud-optimized Game Pass title using Cloud Gaming. This includes big names like:

  • Halo Infinite
  • Forza Horizon 5
  • Microsoft Flight Simulator
  • Fortnite
  • Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six Siege
  • Grand Theft Auto V
  • Among Us
  • Sea of Thieves
  • Gears 5
  • Minecraft Dungeons
  • Doom Eternal and more.

To explore the full catalog of cloud-optimized Game Pass titles, visit the Xbox Cloud Gaming library.

With Remote Play, you can stream any game already installed on your Xbox (except backward-compatible and some third-party titles).

Can You Use Touch Controls Instead of a Controller?

Yes, but only for select titles. Look for the Play with Touch section in Xbox Cloud Gaming. Games like Minecraft Dungeons and Hades support this. Touch controls are generally not supported in Remote Play. A compatible controller is typically required.

How to Connect an Xbox Controller to an iPhone or iPad

To play Xbox games smoothly, you’ll need to connect a supported controller to your iPhone or iPad. Here’s how to pair your Xbox Wireless Controller:

  1. Go to Settings > Bluetooth on your iPhone or iPad.

  2. Turn on your Xbox controller by pressing the Xbox button.
  3. Hold the pair button until it blinks.
  4. On your iOS device, tap Xbox Wireless Controller under Bluetooth devices.

You can also use PlayStation DualSense, Razer Kishi, and mobile clips like 8BitDo for comfort.

Best iPhone and iPad Models for Xbox Gaming

For optimal Xbox Cloud and Remote Play gaming on iPhones and iPads, prioritize devices with powerful processors, high-refresh-rate displays, and reliable connectivity.

We recommend using any iPhone model above the iPhone 12 (excluding SE models) and any iPad model newer than the iPad Pro 2nd Gen. However, even some older models can work just fine as long as they’re updated to the latest iOS or iPadOS version and have a stable internet connection.

Tips for the Best Xbox Gaming Experience on an iPhone and iPad

Want to make sure your Xbox gaming session on iPhone or iPad runs as smoothly as possible? Here are some practical tips to help you get the best performance, visuals, and overall experience:

  • Connect to a 5GHz Wi-Fi network for low latency.
  • Ensure internet speed is at least 10 Mbps.
  • Avoid other high-bandwidth activities like downloading while gaming.
  • Use Xbox Wireless or MFi-certified controllers like Backbone One or Razer Kishi.
  • Add Xbox Cloud Gaming to your Home Screen for quick access.
  • Enable Do Not Disturb to block interruptions.
  • Use the landscape mode for better controls.
  • Close unused apps to free memory.
  • Use a headset for better audio and in-game chat.
  • Keep your device cool to avoid performance throttling.
  • Save your game often. Disconnections are rare, but they can still happen.

The Future of Xbox Gaming on iPhones and iPads

Whether you’re deep into the Xbox ecosystem or just testing the waters, playing Xbox games on your iPhone or iPad opens up a whole new way to game on the go. With Cloud Gaming, you don’t even need a console—just a subscription, decent internet, and a screen. And if you already have an Xbox at home, Remote Play keeps your favorite games close, no matter where you are.

As Microsoft continues to blur the lines between console and cloud, your iPhone or iPad might become your next favorite gaming device. Pair your controller, pick your game, and dive in.

FAQs

Do I need an Xbox console to use Xbox Cloud Gaming?

No. You can stream directly from Microsoft servers using a Game Pass Ultimate subscription.

Is Xbox Game Pass Ultimate Required?

Yes, for Cloud Gaming. The Xbox Game Pass Ultimate gives you access to 100+ games to stream, including EA Play and day-one Xbox Studio titles. Remote Play does not need a Game Pass, just the Xbox app and a console.

Does Xbox Remote Play work over cellular?

Yes, but performance may drop. Use 5GHz Wi-Fi or strong 5G for better results.

Will using a controller drain my iPhone battery?

Slightly. Bluetooth uses some power, but it’s minimal compared to screen brightness and network usage. A full charge before a session is recommended.

mainEntity.name: How often should you replace AirPods Pro tips?

acceptedAnswer.text: AirPods Pro ear tips are durable, but they don’t last forever. Daily use, earwax buildup, sweat, and environmental factors can degrade the silicone over time. It’s best to replace them when you notice wear, discomfort, or a drop in audio performance.

mainEntity.name: How often should I clean AirPods Pro tips?

mainEntity.name: Do I need an Xbox console to use Xbox Cloud Gaming?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. You can stream directly from Microsoft servers using a Game Pass Ultimate subscription.

mainEntity.name: Is Xbox Game Pass Ultimate Required?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for Cloud Gaming. The Xbox Game Pass Ultimate gives you access to 100+ games to stream, including EA Play and day-one Xbox Studio titles. Remote Play does not need a Game Pass, just the Xbox app and a console.

mainEntity.name: Does Xbox Remote Play work over cellular?

@graph.name: How to Play Xbox Games on an iPhone and iPad Using Xbox Cloud Gaming (xCloud)
@graph.description: Stream and play Xbox games on your iPhone or iPad through Xbox Cloud Gaming (xCloud) using Safari and a paired controller. Follow these steps to set it up quickly.

step.name: Go to Xbox Cloud Gaming website
step.text: Open Safari on your iPhone or iPad and go to Xbox’s Cloud Gaming website.

itemListElement.text: Open Safari and go to Xbox’s Cloud Gaming website.

step.name: Sign in with Microsoft account
step.text: Sign in using your Microsoft account that is linked to your Game Pass Ultimate subscription.

itemListElement.text: Sign in using your Microsoft account linked to Game Pass Ultimate.

step.name: Add Cloud Gaming to Home Screen
step.text: Tap the Share icon at the bottom of Safari, select Add to Home Screen, and tap Add.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Share icon at the bottom of Safari.
Select Add to Home Screen.
Tap Add.

step.name: Open Cloud Gaming from Home Screen
step.text: You will now see the Cloud Gaming icon on your Home Screen. Tap it to open the website.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Cloud Gaming icon on your Home Screen.

step.name: Pair your controller
step.text: From your iPhone or iPad Settings app, pair your Xbox controller via Bluetooth.

itemListElement.text: Open the Settings app.
Pair your Xbox controller via Bluetooth.

step.name: Start playing
step.text: Select any game from the Cloud Gaming library and start playing using your paired controller.

itemListElement.text: Tap on a game from the library.
Start playing with your paired controller.

@graph.name: How to Play Xbox Games on an iPhone and iPad Using Remote Play
@graph.description: Stream and play Xbox games installed on your console directly to your iPhone or iPad using the Remote Play feature. This guide shows you how to enable the right settings, connect your controller, and start gaming.

supply.name: Xbox console with Remote Play enabled

step.name: Open Xbox settings
step.text: On your Xbox console, press the Xbox button and go to Profile & System, then select Settings.

itemListElement.text: Press the Xbox button.
Go to Profile & System > Settings.

step.name: Access remote features settings
step.text: Go to Devices & Connections and select Remote Features.

itemListElement.text: Go to Devices & Connections > Remote Features.

step.name: Enable remote play
step.text: Enable Remote Features and set Power Mode to Instant-On to allow quick streaming.

itemListElement.text: Enable Remote Features.
Set Power Mode to Instant-On.

step.name: Launch Xbox app on iPhone or iPad
step.text: Open the Xbox app on your iPhone or iPad and sign in with your Microsoft account.

itemListElement.text: Open the Xbox app on iPhone or iPad.
Sign in with your Microsoft account.

step.name: Start remote play
step.text: In the Xbox app, tap My Library, select Consoles, choose your console, and tap Remote Play on This Device.

itemListElement.text: Tap My Library > Consoles.
Select your console and tap Remote Play on This Device.

step.name: Pair your controller
step.text: Pair your Xbox controller with your iPhone or iPad via Bluetooth from the device's settings.

itemListElement.text: Pair your controller via Bluetooth.

step.name: Start playing
step.text: Launch any installed game on your Xbox remotely and start playing from your iPhone or iPad.

itemListElement.text: Start playing any installed game.

keyPoints.title: Play Xbox Games on iPhone and iPad with Xbox Cloud Gaming
keyPoints.explanation: Using Xbox Cloud Gaming (xCloud), players can stream Xbox titles directly to their iOS devices with a Game Pass Ultimate subscription, no Xbox console needed, via a supported browser and controller.

keyPoints.title: Remote Play to Stream Games from Your Xbox Console
keyPoints.explanation: Xbox Remote Play allows users to stream installed games from their own Xbox console to an iPhone or iPad over the internet, ideal for continuing gameplay remotely from anywhere.

keyPoints.title: Differences Between Cloud Gaming and Remote Play
keyPoints.explanation: Cloud Gaming relies on Microsoft servers and a Game Pass subscription, while Remote Play streams games from your personal console; both require a stable internet connection.

keyPoints.title: Compatible Xbox Games and Using Touch Controls
keyPoints.explanation: Cloud Gaming supports a vast library of Game Pass titles, some with touch controls, whereas Remote Play streams any installed game, typically requiring a controller for input.

keyPoints.title: Connecting Controllers and Optimizing Gaming Experience
keyPoints.explanation: Pair a supported Bluetooth controller like Xbox Wireless Controller to your iOS device for better gameplay, and use tips like connecting to a 5GHz Wi-Fi network for smoother streaming.

title.rendered: Samsung Just Proved Apple’s Foldable iPhone Timing Is Right

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 7 and Flip 7 hit record demand as pre-orders surge and refined designs show foldables are finally resonating with mainstream buyers.
  • Apple’s 2026 foldable launch rides on market maturity, using extra time to avoid early-stage issues and deliver a more reliable, polished first-gen product.
  • Six generations of Samsung foldables improved durability and usability, proving slow iteration works and setting consumer expectations for future foldable launches.
  • Apple’s delay looks more strategic than hesitant, giving it space to learn from rivals and avoid launching a fragile or gimmicky device too early.
  • Future foldable iPhone buyers should still expect limitations, especially around price and form factor tradeoffs, even with Apple’s typically refined execution.

Apple’s long-rumored foldable iPhone is now expected in 2026, a full seven years after Samsung introduced the original Galaxy Fold. On the surface, that might sound like a late entry. But Samsung’s own positioning around its latest generation of foldables suggests Apple may be stepping in right on time.

Samsung: Foldables Are Finally Mainstream

Samsung says demand for its new Galaxy Z Fold 7 and Z Flip 7 has hit record levels in the U.S., signaling a broader shift in consumer acceptance of foldable smartphones:

  • Combined pre-orders are up 25% over last year.
  • Carrier pre-orders have surged by 60%.
  • The Fold 7 alone is outselling the Fold 6 by 50%, making it the best-performing Z Fold to date.

That marks a major turnaround from early models, which were hampered by screen failures, bulky designs, and uncertain market appeal. Drew Blackard, Samsung’s SVP of Mobile Product Management, says

Foldables have now reached an “inflection point” where they are truly mainstream.. Years of feedback have shaped the design, durability, and software to a point where the experience clicks for users. When people go hands-on with a Z series device, they’re hooked

This evolution underlines why Apple’s 2026 timeline might actually be strategic. Rather than entering during the experimental phase, Apple will launch into a segment that’s had time to stabilize, where foldables are no longer a curiosity but a category with proven traction. That gives Apple the opportunity to bypass years of trial-and-error and focus instead on polish and refinement from the outset.

Why Apple Might Be Right to Wait

Samsung’s seventh-gen devices finally deliver what early adopters were asking for all along: thinner builds, better durability, and a more confident design language. But it took six generations of incremental improvements, user feedback, and public missteps to get there.

Critics have called Apple late to the foldables race. But the more accurate read might be that Apple has waited until the race reached the stadium. With hardware more reliable and software use cases more defined, the market has matured enough for a company like Apple to enter with a product that doesn’t feel like a science project.

Assuming current reports hold, the first iPhone Fold will launch into a market that’s ready. That gives Apple the breathing room to deliver something closer to a complete product, not a beta test wrapped in premium pricing. Historically, Apple has made similar late-move bets work before. And this timing could be less about delay and more about calculated patience.

Would you buy a foldable iPhone in 2026, or is Apple still too late to the party? Sound off in the comments.

Don’t miss these related reads:

  • Apple’s First Foldable iPhone Could Launch in 2026 at $1,999
  • Foldable iPhone Said to Feature Crease-Free Display From Samsung
  • iPhone Fold 1 Could Be Thinner and Cheaper Than Expected

title.rendered: How to Delete YouTube Search History – iPhone, Android and Desktop

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Deletion Options: On mobile, you can delete individual searches, clear by date, or delete your entire Youtube history.
  • Delete Single Searches: To delete a single search, swipe left on iOS or long-press on Android and tap “Remove.”
  • Deleting by Date: Deleting searches by a specific date range also deletes your watch history from that same time period.
  • Deleting All History: Clearing your entire search history will also permanently delete your entire YouTube watch history at the same time.
  • Pausing History: In your account settings, you can pause your search history to prevent future searches from being saved.

Ever searched for something on YouTube that you don’t want lingering around in your history? Maybe it’s a surprise gift tutorial, a health-related search, or just something random you don’t want affecting your recommendations. Thankfully, YouTube makes it easy to delete your search history – whether you’re using an Android device, iPhone, or PC.

Deleting your search history not only removes it from suggestions, helping your privacy, but also stops it from influencing what videos YouTube recommends to you. Here’s how you can clear it quickly on all your devices.

Table of Contents
  • How to Delete YouTube Search History on Mobile? (iPhone and Android)
    • How to Delete YouTube Searches One-by-One? (iPhone and Android)
    • Steps to Delete Search History by Date (iPhone and Android)
    • How to Clear Entire YouTube Search History? (iPhone and Android)
    • How to Pause Search History on YouTube? (iPhone and Android)
    • How to Auto Delete YouTube History? (iPhone and Android)
  • How to Delete YouTube Search History on PC?
    • How to Delete YouTube Searches One-by-One? (Desktop)
    • Steps to Delete Search History by Date (Desktop)
    • How to Clear Entire YouTube Search History? (Desktop)
    • How to Pause Search History on YouTube? (Desktop)
    • How to Auto Delete YouTube History? (Desktop)
  • Incognito Mode: A Quick Alternative

How to Delete YouTube Search History on Mobile? (iPhone and Android)

The method to delete YouTube Search History is the same on both iPhone and Android. Below are all the different ways you can manage your searches.

How to Delete YouTube Searches One-by-One? (iPhone and Android)

If you want to remove specific searches you made, follow these steps:

  1. Open the YouTube app.
  2. Tap on the Search icon.
  3. Swipe left on the search you want to delete (on Android, long-press the search).
  4. Tap the Delete or Remove option to delete that specific search.

Alternatively, you can also delete specific searches from your Google Account Settings page:

  1. Open the YouTube app.
  2. Tap your profile picture/photo at the bottom right.
  3. Tap the Settings icon at the top right.
  4. Select Manage all history option.
  5. Here, you can check your YouTube activity history.
  6. Search for the search you want to delete.
  7. Tap the Delete icon beside that search to remove it.

Steps to Delete Search History by Date (iPhone and Android)

You can clear searches made in a particular date range without deleting everything. However, this method will also delete your watch history for that date, along with the search history. There is no option to delete just the search history.

  1. Open the YouTube app.
  2. Tap your profile picture/photo at the bottom right.
  3. Tap the Settings icon at the top right.
  4. Select Manage all history option.
  5. Tap DELETE and then select Delete custom range from the drop-down.
  6. Select the start date in the After section and end date in the Before section.
  7. You can also set either an after or before date to delete all data before or after that date.
  8. Tap Next.
  9. On the next page, tap Delete to confirm.

How to Clear Entire YouTube Search History? (iPhone and Android)

Want to clear your entire search history at once? Here’s how. However, similar to deleting by custom date, deleting your entire search history will also delete your entire watch history. There is no way to delete just the search history.

  1. Open the YouTube app.
  2. Tap your profile picture/photo at the bottom right.
  3. Tap the Settings icon at the top right.
  4. Select Manage all history option.
  5. Tap DELETE and then select Delete all time from the drop-down.
  6. On the next page, tap Delete again to confirm.

How to Pause Search History on YouTube? (iPhone and Android)

If you don’t want YouTube to save your searches in the first place, you can pause it. Any searches you make later will not be saved in your history.

  1. Open the YouTube app.
  2. Tap your profile picture/photo at the bottom right.
  3. Tap the Settings icon at the top right.
  4. Select Manage all history option.
  5. Go to the Controls tab.
  6. Unselect Include your searches on YouTube.

That’s it, you have successfully turned off the search history on YouTube. You can enable this toggle anytime to start saving your search history again.

How to Auto Delete YouTube History? (iPhone and Android)

You can also set YouTube to auto-delete your search history regularly.

  1. Open the YouTube app.
  2. Tap your profile picture/photo at the bottom right.
  3. Tap the Settings icon at the top right.
  4. Select Manage all history option.
  5. Go to the Controls tab.
  6. Tap on Choose an auto-delete option. 
  7. Choose to auto-delete your YouTube search history every 3, 18, or 36 months.
  8. If you prefer keeping your history, select Don’t auto-delete activity.
  9. Once done, tap on Next and then Confirm. 

How to Delete YouTube Search History on PC?

On your computer, you can manage your YouTube search history through the My Activity page. Here’s how.

How to Delete YouTube Searches One-by-One? (Desktop)

To remove specific searches from your history:

  1. Open YouTube and click on the Search bar. 
  2. Now, hover over the suggestion that you want to remove 
  3. Click on cross icon on the right to delete that specific search. 

Alternatively, you can also delete from YouTube My Activity page. 

  1. Visit the YouTube My Activity page. Confirm you are using the correct account. 
  2. Scroll to find the search you want to delete.
  3. Click the Delete icon beside it.

Steps to Delete Search History by Date (Desktop)

You can clear searches made in a particular date range without deleting everything. However, this method will also delete your watch history for that date, along with the search history. There is no option to delete just the search history.

  1. Visit the YouTube My Activity page. Confirm you are using the correct account. 
  2. Click Delete and then select Delete custom range from the drop-down.
  3. Select the start date in the After section and end date in the Before section.
  4. You can also set either an after or before date to delete all data before or after that date.
  5. Click Next.
  6. On the next page, click Delete to confirm.

How to Clear Entire YouTube Search History? (Desktop)

Want to clear your entire search history at once? Here’s how. However, similar to deleting by custom date, deleting your entire search history will also delete your entire watch history. There is no way to delete just the search history.

  1. Visit the YouTube My Activity page. Confirm you are using the correct account. 
  2. Click DELETE and then select Delete all time from the drop-down.
  3. On the next page, tap Delete again to confirm.

How to Pause Search History on YouTube? (Desktop)

To stop YouTube from saving your searches temporarily:

  1. Visit the YouTube My Activity page. Confirm you are using the correct account. 
  2. Select Controls option in the left sidebar.
  3. Unselect Include your searches on YouTube.

How to Auto Delete YouTube History? (Desktop)

You can also set YouTube to auto-delete your search history regularly.

  1. Visit the YouTube My Activity page. Confirm you are using the correct account. 
  2. Select Controls option in the left sidebar.
  3. Click on Choose an auto-delete option. 
  4. Choose to auto-delete your YouTube search history every 3, 18, or 36 months.
  5. If you prefer keeping your history, select Don’t auto-delete activity.
  6. Once done, click on Next and then Confirm.

Incognito Mode: A Quick Alternative

Remember, if you don’t want YouTube to save your searches at all for a while, you can use Incognito mode. When browsing in Incognito, your searches and watched videos won’t be saved to your history.

Deleting your search history is a simple way to keep your YouTube experience private and your recommendations clean. Whether it’s on your phone or desktop, you’re just a few taps away from clearing it out and starting fresh.

  • How to Turn Off Autoplay on YouTube

@graph.name: How to Delete YouTube Search History on iPhone or Android
@graph.description: Clear your YouTube search history on iPhone or Android using the app’s Manage All History settings for better privacy and recommendations.

step.name: Open the YouTube app
step.text: Launch the YouTube app on your iPhone or Android device.

itemListElement.text: Tap the YouTube icon from your home screen or app drawer.

step.name: Go to your profile
step.text: Tap your profile picture or photo at the bottom right corner of the app.

itemListElement.text: Select your profile icon from the navigation bar.

step.name: Open YouTube settings
step.text: Tap the settings icon at the top right of your profile page.

itemListElement.text: Tap the gear icon to open settings.

step.name: Manage history
step.text: Select Manage all history from the available settings.

itemListElement.text: Tap Manage all history to open your YouTube activity page.

step.name: Delete all search history
step.text: Tap DELETE and choose Delete all time from the drop-down menu.

itemListElement.text: Tap DELETE and select Delete all time.

step.name: Confirm deletion
step.text: On the next page, tap Delete again to confirm clearing your search history.

itemListElement.text: Tap Delete to finalize the process.

step.name: Open YouTube
step.text: Go to the YouTube website and click on the search bar to display recent search suggestions.

itemListElement.text: Open YouTube in your preferred browser.
Click inside the search bar to view recent searches.

step.name: Find the search to delete
step.text: Hover your cursor over the suggestion you want to remove from your search history.

itemListElement.text: Move your cursor over the unwanted search term.

step.name: Delete the search entry
step.text: Click the cross icon on the right to remove that specific search from your history.

itemListElement.text: Click the X icon next to the search term to delete it.

@graph.name: How to Delete YouTube Search History by Date on Desktop or Mac
@graph.description: Delete YouTube search history for a specific date range on Desktop or Mac by using the custom range option in the My Activity page.

step.name: Go to YouTube My Activity
step.text: Visit the YouTube My Activity page and make sure you are signed in to the correct account.

itemListElement.text: Open your browser and go to myactivity.google.com.
Check that you are signed into the right Google account.

step.name: Open delete options
step.text: Click Delete and choose Delete custom range from the drop-down menu.

itemListElement.text: Click the Delete button.
Select Delete custom range from the list.

step.name: Set date range
step.text: Select the start date in the After section and the end date in the Before section. You can also choose only one date to delete all activity before or after that date.

itemListElement.text: Pick a start date under After.
Pick an end date under Before.
Optionally, set only one date for partial deletion.

step.name: Confirm deletion
step.text: Click Next, then click Delete on the confirmation page to remove the history for the selected date range.

itemListElement.text: Click Next to proceed.
Click Delete to finalize.

@graph.name: How to Delete YouTube Search History on Desktop or Mac
@graph.description: Clear your entire YouTube search history on Desktop or Mac via the YouTube My Activity page using the Delete All Time option.

step.name: Go to YouTube My Activity
step.text: Visit the YouTube My Activity page and confirm you are signed into the correct Google account.

itemListElement.text: Open your browser and navigate to myactivity.google.com.
Check that the signed-in account is the one you want to manage.

step.name: Select Delete All Time
step.text: Click DELETE and choose Delete all time from the drop-down list.

itemListElement.text: Click the DELETE button.
Select Delete all time from the menu.

step.name: Confirm deletion
step.text: On the confirmation page, click Delete again to permanently remove all YouTube search history.

itemListElement.text: Review the confirmation screen.
Click Delete to finalize the process.

@graph.name: How to Auto Delete YouTube Search History on Desktop or Mac
@graph.description: Automatically clear your YouTube search history on Desktop or Mac at regular intervals by setting an auto-delete preference in the My Activity settings.

step.name: Go to YouTube My Activity
step.text: Visit the YouTube My Activity page and make sure you are signed in to the correct Google account.

itemListElement.text: Open your preferred web browser.
Go to myactivity.google.com and confirm your account.

step.name: Open Controls
step.text: Select the Controls option from the left sidebar.

itemListElement.text: In the left-hand menu, click Controls.

step.name: Choose auto-delete option
step.text: Click on Choose an auto-delete option to manage your YouTube search history settings.

itemListElement.text: Click Choose an auto-delete option in the settings.

step.name: Select auto-delete frequency
step.text: Choose to auto-delete your YouTube search history every 3, 18, or 36 months. If you want to keep all history, select Don’t auto-delete activity.

itemListElement.text: Select your preferred interval: 3, 18, or 36 months.
Select Don’t auto-delete activity if you want to keep all search history.

step.name: Save changes
step.text: Click Next and then Confirm to apply your auto-delete settings.

itemListElement.text: Click Next to continue.
Click Confirm to save your settings.

@graph.name: How To Pause YouTube Search History on Desktop or Mac
@graph.description: Learn how to quickly pause your YouTube search history on a desktop or Mac so your searches aren’t saved to your Google account.

step.name: Go to YouTube My Activity page
step.text: Open your browser and visit the YouTube My Activity page, making sure you are signed in to the correct account.

itemListElement.text: Visit the YouTube My Activity page.
Confirm you are using the correct Google account.

step.name: Adjust search history controls
step.text: From the left sidebar, select the Controls option, then uncheck the box for Include your searches on YouTube to pause search history.

itemListElement.text: Select Controls from the left sidebar.
Unselect Include your searches on YouTube.

keyPoints.title: Easy steps to delete YouTube Search History on mobile
keyPoints.explanation: You can manage your searches on both iPhone and Android by deleting individual searches, clearing by date, or deleting all at once, through simple in-app steps.

keyPoints.title: How to delete searches one-by-one on mobile devices
keyPoints.explanation: Swipe left on a search (or long-press on Android) in the YouTube app and tap delete, or remove from your Google Account settings for more control.

keyPoints.title: Clearing search history by date range on mobile
keyPoints.explanation: You can delete searches made within a specific date range via the history settings, but this also deletes watch history for those dates.

keyPoints.title: Removing all search history on mobile devices
keyPoints.explanation: To clear your entire search history, access the account settings and select 'Delete all time,' which also deletes your watch history.

keyPoints.title: Pausing search history to prevent saving future searches
keyPoints.explanation: Disable the option in YouTube settings under 'Manage all history' to stop saving searches temporarily on both mobile and desktop.

title.rendered: Apple Ships 3 Billion iPhones as Q3 2025 Earnings Top Estimates

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple hits 3 billion iPhones shipped since 2007 after nearly two decades, reflecting how central the iPhone remains in Apple’s long-term strategy.
  • iPhone shipment pace is accelerating with 1 billion units shipped between 2021 and 2025, compared to the 9 years it took to reach the first billion.
  • Milestone reveals rare sales insight post-2018 as Apple no longer shares quarterly iPhone numbers, making this a key pulse check for investors.
  • iPhone’s evolution has fueled demand with hallmark upgrades like Face ID, 5G, and Dynamic Island sustaining buyer interest across generations.
  • Apple expects AI and foldables to boost future sales with Apple Intelligence and foldable iPhone speculation seen as critical to the next growth wave.

Apple’s Q3 2025 earnings are in, and the company has once again outperformed Wall Street expectations. The quarter delivered stronger-than-anticipated iPhone revenue, a new high for its Services business, and healthy earnings per share, even as Apple continues to navigate international tariffs and mounting regulatory pressure.

Apple Hits 3 Billion iPhones Shipped

During the earnings call, CEO Tim Cook confirmed a major milestone: Apple has officially shipped its three-billionth iPhone since the product first launched in 2007.

The figure underscores not just the iPhone’s scale but also its evolution into the cornerstone of Apple’s ecosystem, a product line that now anchors everything from services to accessories and continues to fuel the company’s growth.

From Billion One to Billion Three

Apple first crossed the 1 billion iPhones shipped mark back in 2016, just nine years after the original model debuted. At the time, Cook called it

One of the most important, world-changing, and successful products in history.

The company never disclosed when it passed the 2 billion milestone, but industry analysts estimate it occurred around September 2021. If that estimate holds, Apple reached its third billion in under four years, a faster climb that reflects accelerating global adoption.

Why Apple Shared the Number

Since Apple stopped reporting hardware unit sales in November 2018, any official milestone like this carries added weight. Back then, CFO Luca Maestri said that quarterly unit sales “are not representative of the underlying strength of our business.”

So when the CEO calls out a unit number during an earnings call, it signals more than just bragging rights; it gives investors and analysts a rare, concrete data point on iPhone momentum.

18 Years of iPhone Evolution

The iPhone’s journey spans nearly two decades of hardware and software shifts:

  • 2007: Original iPhone launched with a 3.5-inch screen and multitouch interface.
  • 2010: iPhone 4 introduced Retina Display and FaceTime.
  • 2014: iPhone 6 series added larger displays, driving record sales.
  • 2017: iPhone X marked the shift to OLED and Face ID.
  • 2020: iPhone 12 brought 5G across the lineup.
  • 2022: iPhone 14 Pro introduced Dynamic Island and Always-On Display.
  • 2024: iPhone 16 lineup unveiled Apple Intelligence and a 48MP Fusion Camera.
  • 2025: Apple reaches 3 billion iPhones shipped globally.

What Fuels the Next Billion?

Looking ahead, Apple appears to be betting that Apple Intelligence, its generative AI system, will be the main engine behind the next surge in iPhone sales. The company has increasingly framed AI as core to its future offerings, embedding it into iOS, hardware, and services.

Add to that persistent rumors of a foldable iPhone model in development. If Apple manages to ship such a device within the next few years, it could help the company hit 4 billion iPhones shipped as early as 2028.

Q3 2025 by the Numbers

Apple’s latest financials offer a clearer view of what’s powering its current growth:

  • Revenue: $94 billion, up about 10% year over year and well ahead of ~$89B expectations.
  • Earnings per Share: $1.57, beating forecasts of $1.42–$1.43 by roughly 12%.
  • iPhone Revenue: $44.6 billion, up 13%, boosted in part by early demand before expected tariff hikes.
  • Services Revenue: $27.4 billion, up 13%, marking a new all-time high.
  • Tariff Impact: $800 million in Q3; Apple expects $1.1B in Q4 and is ramping up production shifts to India and Vietnam.

Looking Forward

Despite legal headwinds and rising trade costs, Apple is entering its next fiscal quarter with momentum. The milestone of 3 billion iPhones shipped, combined with a strong Q3 and growing focus on AI and new form factors like the rumored iPhone Fold, points to a company still expanding its playbook.

Whether Apple Intelligence and a foldable iPhone can meaningfully accelerate sales remains to be seen. Would either push you to upgrade? Let us know in the comments.

excerpt.rendered: Apple hits 3 billion iPhones shipped and beats Q3 2025 estimates, thanks to iPhone 16 sales and record-breaking Services revenue. Here’s what it means for the future.

keyPoints.title: Apple Achieves a Major Milestone with 3 Billion iPhones Shipped
keyPoints.explanation: CEO Tim Cook announced that Apple has shipped its three-billionth iPhone since 2007, highlighting the device's crucial role in Apple's ecosystem and growth.

keyPoints.title: Rapid Growth in iPhone Shipments Since 2016
keyPoints.explanation: After surpassing 1 billion units in 2016, Apple likely hit 2 billion around 2021, and reaching 3 billion in under four years demonstrates accelerating global adoption.

keyPoints.title: Importance of Sharing Shipment Numbers
keyPoints.explanation: Since Apple stopped reporting quarterly hardware sales in 2018, announcing shipment milestones offers investors a rare insight into iPhone momentum and company health.

keyPoints.title: 18 Years of iPhone Evolution
keyPoints.explanation: The iPhone has evolved through nearly two decades, introducing innovations like Retina display, Face ID, 5G, and Dynamic Island, shaping its continual growth.

keyPoints.title: Future Growth Drivers: AI and Foldable iPhone Rumors
keyPoints.explanation: Apple foresees AI, especially Apple Intelligence, and potentially a foldable iPhone as the main engines for reaching the next billion in shipped units.

title.rendered: How to Make a Conference Call on iPhone: A Complete Guide

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • The Basics: Making conference calls on an iPhone is simple and gives you full control without needing third-party apps.
  • Prerequisites: Before calling, ensure your carrier supports conference calls and that you have a strong cellular signal.
  • How to Make the Call: Start by calling one person, then tap “Add Call” for the next participant and finally “Merge Calls.”
  • In-Call Management: As the host, you can speak privately with one person or remove participants directly from the call screen.
  • New in iOS 26: The upcoming iOS 26 update will introduce features like real-time translation and advanced call screening.

Conference calls are a fantastic way to bring people together—whether it’s for work, family catch-ups, or planning events. If you use an iPhone, you’ll be glad to know that setting up and managing a conference call is incredibly simple with the built-in Phone app. In this guide, I’ll walk you through how to make a conference call on iPhone, including requirements, benefits, step-by-step instructions, and pro tips.

Table of Contents
  • Benefits of Using iPhone for Conference Calls
  • Requirements Before Starting a Conference Call
  • How to Make a Conference Call on iPhone
    • Step 1: Call the First Person
    • Step 2: Add Another Call
    • Step 3: Dial the Second Person
    • Step 4: Merge the Calls
  • How to Conduct a Private Conversation
  • How to Remove Someone From a Conference Call
  • What's New in iOS 26 for Conference Calls?
  • Tips for Smooth Conference Calling on iPhone
  • Troubleshooting iPhone Conference Calling Issues

    Benefits of Using iPhone for Conference Calls

    Using your iPhone for group calls offers several advantages:

    • No third-party apps needed – Use the built-in Phone app.
    • Add up to five participants (carrier-dependent).
    • Full control – Use speaker, mute, or private chat options.
    • No extra cost – If supported by your carrier, there are no extra charges.

    In short, conference calling on an iPhone is intuitive and efficient.

    Requirements Before Starting a Conference Call

    Before placing a group call, ensure the following:

    1. Carrier support: Most major U.S. carriers like Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile support conference calls. However, check if your specific plan allows it.
    2. Strong signal: A solid cellular connection is essential for clear audio.
    3. Latest iOS version: Update your iPhone to ensure access to the latest features.
    4. Participant details ready: Have phone numbers on hand to avoid delays.
    5. Disable VoLTE or Wi-Fi Calling (if needed): These can interfere with call merging. Go to Settings > Cellular > Wi-Fi Calling and toggle it off if you face issues.

    How to Make a Conference Call on iPhone

    Follow these steps to make and manage a conference call:

    Step 1: Call the First Person

    • Open the Phone app and dial the first number or select a contact. Wait for them to answer.

    Step 2: Add Another Call

    • Tap the Add Call button. This puts the first person on hold.

    Step 3: Dial the Second Person

    • Choose another contact or enter the second number. Tap the Call button and wait for them to answer.

    Step 4: Merge the Calls

    • Once the second call connects, tap Merge Calls. You’ll now have a three-way call. Repeat steps 2–4 to add more participants (up to five, based on your carrier).

    Pro Tip If someone calls you during a conference, tap Hold & Accept, then tap Merge Calls to include them.

    How to Conduct a Private Conversation

    Need to speak to someone privately during a conference call?

    1. During the conference call, tap the (i) button at the top of the call screen.
    2. Find the participant’s name or number, then tap Private below. This puts the other participants on hold.
    3. When you’re done, tap Merge Calls to bring everyone back into the group conversation.

    Note Only the person who started the call can use the Private feature. It may not be supported by all carriers.

    How to Remove Someone From a Conference Call

    You can easily remove a participant:

    1. Tap the (i) button to view the participant list.
    2. Tap End next to the participant’s name to disconnect them.
    3. To end the entire call, tap the red End Call button.

    Only the call initiator can remove individual participants.

    What’s New in iOS 26 for Conference Calls?

    Apple has made some exciting improvements in iOS 26:

    iOS 26 introduces several updates to iPhone call management that can improve your conference call experience:

    • Live Translation: Apple Intelligence can now translate conversations in real time with on-screen captions.
    • Call Screening: Your iPhone can automatically answer unknown calls and ask for the caller’s name before letting you decide whether to answer.

    To enable these features, go to Settings > General > Software Update and install the latest version of iOS 26.

    Related: How to Download iOS 26 Developer Beta on iPhone

    Tips for Smooth Conference Calling on iPhone

    Want a better group call experience? Try these tips:

    • Plan your call and keep contact info handy.
    • Use headphones with a built-in mic for clearer audio.
    • Choose a quiet, strong-signal location.
    • Tap Mute when you’re not speaking to reduce background noise.
    • Use Speaker mode wisely to avoid echo.
    • Practice using Merge and Add Call features before an important call.
    • Keep groups under five people for better clarity and control.

    Troubleshooting iPhone Conference Calling Issues

    If you encounter problems during a conference call, try these solutions: 

    Make Conference Calls Like a Pro!

    That’s everything you need to know about making a conference call on your iPhone. It’s fast, reliable, and packed with features—even more so with iOS 26. Whether you’re catching up with friends, hosting a remote team meeting, or managing a project, your iPhone has you covered.

    Have questions or facing issues? Drop a comment—I’m here to help!

    FAQs

    Why can’t I merge calls on my iPhone?

    You might be using a carrier or plan that doesn’t support merging calls. Also, VoLTE or Wi-Fi Calling can interfere. Disable them via Settings > Cellular > Wi-Fi Calling, or contact your carrier.

    Can I make conference calls on iPad?

    Yes—if your iPad supports cellular calling. Otherwise, use FaceTime or third-party apps like Zoom for group calls on Wi-Fi-only iPads.

    Can I schedule a conference call?

    The iPhone’s native Phone app doesn’t offer scheduling. You can use FaceTime, Zoom, or Microsoft Teams, or set a reminder in Calendar.

    What are the best third-party apps for conference calling?

    For larger or more advanced calls, try apps like Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, or OpenPhone. You can download these from the App Store.

    Read more:

    • What is Call Waiting on iPhone and how to Activate It
    • What Does Cancelled Call Mean on iPhone and How to Fix It!
    • How to fix “Call Failed” error on iPhone

blockGraphs.question: Why can't I merge calls on my iPhone?
blockGraphs.answer: You might be using a carrier or plan that doesn't support merging calls. Also, VoLTE or Wi-Fi Calling can interfere. Disable them via Settings > Cellular > Wi-Fi Calling, or contact your carrier.

blockGraphs.question: Can I make conference calls on iPad?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes—if your iPad supports cellular calling. Otherwise, use FaceTime or third-party apps like Zoom for group calls on Wi-Fi-only iPads.

blockGraphs.question: Can I schedule a conference call?
blockGraphs.answer: The iPhone's native Phone app doesn't offer scheduling. You can use FaceTime, Zoom, or Microsoft Teams, or set a reminder in Calendar.

blockGraphs.question: What are the best third-party apps for conference calling?
blockGraphs.answer: For larger or more advanced calls, try apps like Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, or OpenPhone. You can download these from the App Store.

keyPoints.title: Advantages of Using iPhone for Conference Calls
keyPoints.explanation: Using an iPhone for group calls is simple, cost-effective, and offers full control with features like mute and speaker options, without needing third-party apps.

keyPoints.title: Prerequisites for Setting Up a Conference Call
keyPoints.explanation: Ensure your carrier supports conference calls, have a strong signal, update to the latest iOS, and gather participant details before starting.

keyPoints.title: Step-by-Step Guide to Making a Conference Call on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Initiate the call by calling the first person, then add more participants using the 'Add Call' feature, and merge calls to create a group conversation.

keyPoints.title: Managing Private Conversations and Participant Removal
keyPoints.explanation: You can privately chat with a participant by putting others on hold and remove participants if you're the call initiator, using the iPhone controls.

keyPoints.title: New Features in iOS 26 Enhancing Conference Calls
keyPoints.explanation: iOS 26 introduces real-time translation and call screening, improving the overall experience of managing and participating in conference calls.

title.rendered: How to Delete Your Snapchat Account (Step-by-Step Guide)

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • The 30-Day Rule: Deleting your account starts a 30-day deactivation period, after which your data is permanently erased.
  • Before You Delete: Before deleting, decide if it’s permanent and consider backing up important data like your Memories first.
  • How to Back Up: You can request and download a backup of your data, like your chat history and Memories.
  • How to Delete: To delete your account, go to Settings, select ‘Delete Account,’ and follow the on-screen confirmation steps.
  • Reactivating Your Account: You can easily reactivate your account by logging back in anytime within the 30-day deactivation window.

Ever felt like Snapchat just isn’t your vibe anymore? Maybe you’re tired of streak pressures, constant notifications, or just want a digital detox. Deleting your Snapchat account sounds simple, but there’s a catch—if you don’t do it right, your data could still be hanging around.

In this guide, I’ll walk you through exactly how to delete your Snapchat account step by step, what happens afterward, and what to consider before you hit that final delete button.

Table of Contents
  • What Happens When You Delete Your Snapchat Account?
  • Things to Consider Before Deleting Snapchat
  • Backup Your Snapchat Data First
    • On Desktop
    • On Android and iPhone
  • How to Delete Your Snapchat Account on iPhone or Android
  • How to Delete Your Snapchat Account on Desktop
  • How to Reactivate a Deleted Snapchat Account
  • Alternatives to Deleting Snapchat

What Happens When You Delete Your Snapchat Account?

Before you go, it’s important to understand what deleting your Snapchat account actually means:

  • Your account enters a 30-day deactivation period.
  • During this time, friends can’t view or contact you.
  • If you log back in within 30 days, Snapchat reactivates your account.
  • After 30 days, your account and data are permanently deleted.

There’s no “pause” or temporary deactivation option like on Instagram or Facebook. Deleting means wiping out:

  • Chats and Snaps
  • Memories
  • Bitmoji
  • Friends list
  • Account settings

So, if you want to save any of that, back up your data first.

Things to Consider Before Deleting Snapchat

Ask yourself these questions before pulling the plug:

  • Do you want a temporary break or a permanent exit?
  • Are you okay with losing all Snaps, chats, and Memories?
  • Have you backed up important content you might want later?

If you’re not 100% sure, you may want to just log out or delete the app for now. But if you’re all in, here’s how to back up your Snapchat data and move forward.

Backup Your Snapchat Data First

Deleting removes all your Snapchat data. If you want to keep your Memories, chats, and other content safe, you can back it up before deleting your account.

On Desktop

Here’s how to back up your Snapchat data using a desktop:

  1. Visit the Snapchat accounts portal and log in.
  2. Click My Data.
  3. In the Select data to include section, checkmark or toggle all data you want to download.
  4. Scroll down and click Next.
  5. On the next page, choose a specific timeline if needed.
  6. Click Submit.
  7. Snapchat will email you a download link.

On Android and iPhone

Here’s how to back up your Snapchat data using your phone:

  1. Open the Snapchat app and tap your profile icon at the top left.
  2. Tap the cogwheel icon at the top right to open Settings.
  3. Scroll down to the Privacy Control section.
  4. Tap My Data.
  5. Select all data you want to download and tap Next.
  6. On the next page, select the time range of data you want to export.
  7. Tap Submit.
  8. You’ll get a confirmation message, and Snapchat will email you the download link shortly.

Want a more detailed breakdown? Here’s our full guide to downloading Snapchat data.

How to Delete Your Snapchat Account on iPhone or Android

To delete your Snapchat account from the mobile app:

  1. Open Snapchat and tap your profile or Bitmoji icon at the top left.
  2. Tap the cogwheel icon at the top right to open Settings.
  3. Scroll down and select Delete account at the bottom of the My Account section.
  4. This will redirect you to the Snapchat website. Sign in again.
  5. Re-enter your account credentials on the Delete Account page.
  6. Tap Continue, and you’ll see Account Deactivated.

How to Delete Your Snapchat Account on Desktop

Prefer doing it on a computer? Follow these steps:

  1. Visit the Snapchat accounts portal and log in to your Snapchat account.
  2. Scroll down and click on Delete My Account.

  3. Enter your username and password to confirm.
  4. Click Continue. Your account will now be deactivated for 30 days before permanent deletion.

How to Reactivate a Deleted Snapchat Account

If you regret deleting Snapchat, you can recover your account within 30 days:

  • Open the Snapchat app.
  • Log in with your username (email/phone won’t work during deactivation).
  • Tap Yes to confirm reactivation.
  • Wait for Snapchat to restore your account – it might take a few minutes to a few hours.

After 30 days, you won’t be able to recover your account—it’s gone forever.

Alternatives to Deleting Snapchat

Not ready to say goodbye for good? You can take a break without permanently deleting your account. Try these options instead:

  1. Log Out of Snapchat: Simply logging out can give you space without deleting your account. You can log back in anytime.
  2. Delete the App: Removing the app stops notifications and prevents endless scrolling. Your account remains safe, and you can reinstall whenever you’re ready.
  3. Mute Notifications: If notifications are overwhelming, turn them off in your phone’s settings or within Snapchat’s notification settings.
  4. Turn Off Background Data: Save data and battery by restricting Snapchat from running in the background.

These small changes can give you the break you need, without erasing your Snapchat presence forever.

FAQs

Can I skip the 30-day deactivation and delete Snapchat instantly?

No. Snapchat requires a 30-day deactivation period before final deletion.

Will my friends be notified if I delete my account?

No direct notification is sent, but your name will disappear from their chat and friends list.

Can I delete Snapchat without knowing my password?

No. You’ll need your password to delete the account. If you forgot it, reset it first before continuing.

  • How to use My AI in Snapchat on iPhone
  • How to remove a friend on Snapchat (3 easy ways)

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Snapchat requires a 30-day deactivation period before final deletion.

mainEntity.name: Will my friends be notified if I delete my account?

acceptedAnswer.text: No direct notification is sent, but your name will disappear from their chat and friends list.

@graph.name: How to Backup Snapchat Data on Desktop
@graph.description: Download a backup of your Snapchat data on desktop using the Snapchat accounts portal to keep a copy of your personal information, messages, and media.

step.name: Log in to the Snapchat accounts portal
step.text: Visit the Snapchat accounts portal in your desktop browser and log in with your account credentials.

itemListElement.text: Go to accounts.snapchat.com in your web browser.
Enter your Snapchat username and password.

step.name: Open My Data
step.text: Click My Data from the available options to view your data download settings.

itemListElement.text: Click on My Data in the menu.

step.name: Select data to include
step.text: In the Select data to include section, checkmark or toggle all the data you want to download.

itemListElement.text: Checkmark the boxes next to the data categories you want.

step.name: Proceed to the next step
step.text: Scroll down and click Next to continue with the backup process.

itemListElement.text: Scroll to the bottom and click the Next button.

step.name: Choose a specific timeline
step.text: If needed, choose a specific timeline for the data you want to download.

itemListElement.text: Select a date range for the backup.

step.name: Submit your request
step.text: Click Submit to request your Snapchat data download.

itemListElement.text: Click Submit to finalize your request.

step.name: Download your data
step.text: Snapchat will send you a download link via email when your data is ready.

itemListElement.text: Check your email for the download link from Snapchat.
Click the link to download your backup.

@graph.name: How to Backup Snapchat Data on Android or iPhone
@graph.description: Download and back up your Snapchat data on Android or iPhone directly from the app using the My Data option in Privacy Controls.

step.name: Open Snapchat and go to your profile
step.text: Open the Snapchat app and tap your profile icon in the top left corner.

itemListElement.text: Tap your profile picture or Bitmoji at the top left.

step.name: Go to Settings
step.text: Tap the cogwheel icon at the top right to open Snapchat settings.

itemListElement.text: Select the settings icon in the top-right corner.

step.name: Open My Data
step.text: Scroll down to the Privacy Control section and tap My Data.

itemListElement.text: Scroll until you find My Data and tap it.

step.name: Select data to download
step.text: Select all the data you want to download and tap Next.

itemListElement.text: Checkmark all the data categories you want to export.
Tap Next to continue.

step.name: Set a time range
step.text: Choose the time range of the data you want to export.

itemListElement.text: Select a specific date range or choose all time.

step.name: Submit your request
step.text: Tap Submit to send a request for your data download.

itemListElement.text: Press the Submit button to confirm.

step.name: Download your Snapchat data
step.text: Snapchat will email you a download link shortly after your request is processed.

itemListElement.text: Open your email and click the link from Snapchat to download your data.

@graph.name: How to Delete Snapchat Account on iPhone or Android
@graph.description: Permanently delete your Snapchat account from iPhone or Android by accessing the Delete Account option in settings and confirming your credentials.

step.name: Open Snapchat and go to your profile
step.text: Open Snapchat and tap your profile or Bitmoji icon at the top left.

itemListElement.text: Tap your profile picture or Bitmoji in the top left corner of the app.

step.name: Go to Settings
step.text: Tap the cogwheel icon at the top right to open Snapchat settings.

itemListElement.text: Tap the gear icon in the top-right corner of your profile screen.

step.name: Select Delete Account
step.text: Scroll down and tap Delete Account at the bottom of the My Account section.

itemListElement.text: Scroll to the My Account section.
Tap Delete Account.

step.name: Sign in on Snapchat’s website
step.text: You’ll be redirected to Snapchat’s website. Sign in with your account credentials again.

itemListElement.text: Enter your Snapchat username and password on the web page.

step.name: Confirm deletion
step.text: Re-enter your account credentials on the Delete Account page and tap Continue to confirm. You’ll see the Account Deactivated screen.

itemListElement.text: Re-enter your Snapchat username and password.
Tap Continue to delete your account.

@graph.name: How to Delete Snapchat Account on Desktop
@graph.description: Permanently delete your Snapchat account from a desktop browser by accessing the accounts portal and confirming your credentials.

step.name: Log in to the Snapchat accounts portal
step.text: Visit the Snapchat accounts portal and log in to your account using your username and password.

itemListElement.text: Open your preferred browser and go to accounts.snapchat.com.
Enter your Snapchat login credentials.

step.name: Select Delete My Account
step.text: Scroll down and click on Delete My Account from the available options.

itemListElement.text: Locate the Delete My Account section.
Click the Delete My Account button.

step.name: Confirm your credentials
step.text: Enter your username and password again to confirm account deletion.

itemListElement.text: Type in your Snapchat username.
Re-enter your password.

step.name: Deactivate and delete your account
step.text: Click Continue to deactivate your account. It will remain deactivated for 30 days before being permanently deleted.

itemListElement.text: Click Continue to finalize the deletion process.

@graph.name: How to Reactivate Deleted Snapchat Account
@graph.description: Restore your deactivated Snapchat account within 30 days by logging back in with your username and confirming reactivation.

step.name: Open Snapchat
step.text: Launch the Snapchat app on your iPhone or Android device.

itemListElement.text: Locate the Snapchat icon on your home screen and tap it.

step.name: Log in with your username
step.text: Enter your Snapchat username and password to log in. Email or phone number won’t work during deactivation.

itemListElement.text: Type your username instead of email or phone.
Enter your password and tap Log In.

step.name: Confirm reactivation
step.text: Tap Yes when prompted to confirm you want to reactivate your account.

itemListElement.text: When the pop-up appears, tap Yes to proceed.

step.name: Wait for restoration
step.text: Snapchat will begin restoring your account, which may take a few minutes to a few hours.

itemListElement.text: Leave the app open or check back later to access your account.

keyPoints.title: Understanding what happens when you delete Snapchat
keyPoints.explanation: When you delete Snapchat, your account goes through a 30-day deactivation period during which you can reactivate, but after this time, your data is permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.

keyPoints.title: Things to consider before deleting Snapchat
keyPoints.explanation: Decide if you want a temporary break or a permanent exit, consider backing up important data, and be aware that all chats, memories, friends list, and account settings will be lost.

keyPoints.title: How to back up Snapchat data
keyPoints.explanation: You can back up your data via the Snapchat website on desktop or through the app on Android and iPhone, ensuring you save memories and important chats before deletion.

keyPoints.title: Steps to delete Snapchat on iPhone or Android
keyPoints.explanation: Open Snapchat, go to settings, select 'Delete account', log in again, and confirm to deactivate your account, which will then be permanently deleted after 30 days.

keyPoints.title: Reactivating a deleted Snapchat account
keyPoints.explanation: You can restore your account within 30 days of deletion by logging in again, but after this period, the account and its data are irrecoverable.
