title.rendered: How to Sign Out of Mail on iPhone: Easy Steps for All Accounts

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Temporarily Disable Mail: To pause emails, go to Settings > Mail > Accounts and simply toggle off the Mail option.
  • Fully Remove an Account: To fully remove an email account from your iPhone, delete it in Settings > Mail > Accounts.
  • Sign Out of iCloud: To remove an iCloud email, sign out of your Apple ID, which also affects other iCloud services.
  • Sign Out of Gmail App: To sign out of the standalone Gmail app, tap your profile picture and manage accounts directly.
  • Why This Matters: These sign-out methods help you manage privacy, switch accounts, or prepare your device for sale.

Sometimes, you just want a break from a flood of emails on your iPhone. Maybe you switched jobs, changed your primary email, or simply prefer using the Gmail or Outlook app instead of Apple’s Mail app. Whatever the reason, signing out of your Mail app is easy once you understand how it works on the latest iOS.

Table of Contents
  • How to Temporarily Turn Off Email on Your iPhone
  • How to Log Out of the Mail App on iPhone
  • How to Remove Your iCloud Email
  • How to Sign Out from Gmail App on iPhone
  • Final Thoughts

How to Temporarily Turn Off Email on Your iPhone

If you only want to take a short break from seeing emails without deleting your account completely, you can simply turn off the Mail feature for that account. This keeps the account saved on your device for other uses like Contacts or Calendars.

  1. Open Settings on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Apps, then Mail.
  3. Tap Mail Accounts.
  4. Select the email account you want to turn off.
  5. For iCloud accounts, turn off Use on this iPhone. For other accounts, turn off Mail.

Your emails will disappear from the Mail app instantly, but the account remains on your iPhone. This is also useful if you want to stop seeing emails in Mail but still use that account in other apps like Contacts or Calendar. You can re-enable it at any time when you’re ready to use it again.

How to Log Out of the Mail App on iPhone

If you’ve switched to a new email provider or no longer want an account on your iPhone, you can remove it completely.

  1. Go to Settings.
  2. Tap Apps, then Mail.
  3. Tap Mail Accounts.
  4. Select the email account you want to remove.
  5. Tap Delete Account.

This will delete the account from the Mail app and other apps using it, such as Contacts or Calendar. But remember, it only removes it from your iPhone. The actual email account still exists, and you can always add it back later if you change your mind.

Just so you know, the above steps work for third-party email accounts. For iCloud accounts, things work a bit differently.

How to Remove Your iCloud Email

To remove your iCloud email—and your Apple ID entirely—from your device:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap your name at the top.
  3. Scroll down and tap Sign Out.
Important This will remove your entire Apple account from the device. You won’t be able to use it in other apps, access iCloud data such as passwords or files, or locate your phone using Find My until you sign back in.

Use this option only if you’re switching Apple IDs or preparing to sell your device.

How to Sign Out from Gmail App on iPhone

If you use the Gmail app instead of Apple’s Mail app, the sign-out process is different because it’s managed within the app itself.

  1. Open the Gmail app.
  2. Tap your profile picture at the top.
  3. Tap Manage Accounts on this device.
  4. Toggle off the account you want to sign out from, or tap Remove from this device to delete it.

This method offers more control over individual Google accounts without affecting the system-wide settings.

Final Thoughts

At first, signing out of Mail on iPhone can feel confusing because Apple integrates email accounts deeply into iOS. But once you know these simple steps, you can manage your inbox the way you want—whether that’s switching accounts, taking a break from work emails, or removing old accounts that no longer serve you.

  • How to fix the “Cannot Get Mail: The Connection to the Server Failed” error on iPhone
  • How to Create a New iCloud Email Account

mainEntity.name: Why can't I change country in the App Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple's stringent requirements make changing your App Store country harder to ensure a smooth transition and adherence to regional regulations. Each nation has its laws concerning digital media and applications. So, you must meet all the criteria to be able to continue purchasing items from your new country's App Store. Also, Apple doesn't want one to lose credit balance, subscriptions, pre-orders etc. This means that if even one condition is not satisfied, you can't complete the process. To learn more about this, go through what to do before changing your App Store Country or region.

mainEntity.name: How to change App Store country without a credit card?

acceptedAnswer.text: Changing your App Store country without a credit card is possible. When entering payment details, select 'None' as the payment method. This allows you to make the switch without entering a new card. However, you won't be able to make any purchases until you add a valid payment method. If you don't see the None option, maybe you have an unpaid balance or due payments. Also, recurring subscription mandates and Family Sharing prevent you from changing the App Store without a credit card. In such a case, you need to create a new Apple ID in that region.

mainEntity.name: How many times can I change my App Store country?

acceptedAnswer.text: There isn't a clear answer to how many times you can change your App Store country. However, to avoid issues, you should only change the App Store location when you really need to. Creating a new Apple ID with a new billing address can be a significantly better option if you need to change your App Store location frequently.

mainEntity.name: Does changing the App Store region affect any apps from the previous region?

acceptedAnswer.text: Changing the App Store region doesn't directly affect apps from the previous region. You can still use the app if it's already downloaded on your device. However, due to regional restrictions, you might not be able to make new purchases within the app or use all its features.

mainEntity.name: What does Head Tracked mean in Spatial Audio?

acceptedAnswer.text: Head Tracked means the sound adjusts in real time based on how you move your head. So if you turn your head left, the audio stays anchored as if it's still coming from the same direction, creating a more realistic and immersive effect.

mainEntity.name: Why is Dolby Atmos not showing in Apple Music?

acceptedAnswer.text: Make sure Dolby Atmos is turned on by heading to Settings > Apps > Music. Also, ensure you're using compatible headphones and that you're playing a track labeled with the Dolby Atmos badge.

mainEntity.name: Is Dolby Atmos better than Lossless on Apple Music?

acceptedAnswer.text: They're different. Dolby Atmos gives you a 3D surround effect, while Lossless delivers higher sound quality. If your device and headphones support both, you can use both together.

mainEntity.name: Can I still see old messages after turning off DMs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can still see old messages after turning off DMs. Blocking, restricting, or limiting who can message you only affects new incoming messages.

mainEntity.name: Can I limit DMs without going private?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can block message requests from strangers and followers while keeping your profile public.

mainEntity.name: Is there a way to auto-delete DMs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Instagram doesn't offer a built-in feature to automatically delete regular DMs. However, you can use Vanish Mode in one-on-one chats, and messages sent in this mode disappear once they are viewed and the chat is closed.

mainEntity.name: Will someone know if I muted or restricted them?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Instagram does not notify the person when you restrict them.

mainEntity.name: Do Story replies count as DMs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Story replies on Instagram count as direct messages. Even an emoji reaction to a Story is counted as a DM.

@graph.name: How to Temporarily Turn Off Email on Your iPhone
@graph.description: Temporarily disable email on your iPhone by turning off Mail for specific accounts without deleting them.

step.name: Open Settings
step.text: Open the Settings app on your iPhone.

itemListElement.text: Locate the Settings app icon on your home screen.
Tap to open it.

step.name: Go to Mail settings
step.text: Tap Apps, then tap Mail.

itemListElement.text: Scroll down and tap Apps.
Select Mail from the list.

step.name: Open Mail Accounts
step.text: Tap Mail Accounts to see the list of accounts linked to your iPhone.

itemListElement.text: Tap Mail Accounts.

step.name: Select the email account
step.text: Choose the email account you want to temporarily turn off.

itemListElement.text: Tap the account you want to disable.

step.name: Turn off Mail
step.text: For iCloud accounts, turn off 'Use on this iPhone'. For other accounts, turn off the Mail toggle.

itemListElement.text: Toggle off 'Use on this iPhone' for iCloud accounts.
Toggle off 'Mail' for other accounts.

@graph.name: How to Log Out of the Mail App on iPhone
@graph.description: Log out of the Mail app on your iPhone by removing an email account from your device in the Settings app.

step.name: Open Settings
step.text: Go to the Settings app on your iPhone.

itemListElement.text: Locate and open the Settings app from your home screen.

step.name: Access Mail settings
step.text: Tap Apps, then select Mail from the list.

itemListElement.text: Scroll down and tap Apps.
Tap Mail.

step.name: Go to Mail Accounts
step.text: Tap Mail Accounts to see the list of email accounts on your device.

itemListElement.text: Tap Mail Accounts.

step.name: Select the account
step.text: Choose the email account you want to log out from.

itemListElement.text: Tap the account you want to remove.

step.name: Delete the account
step.text: Tap Delete Account to remove it from your iPhone and log out of the Mail app.

itemListElement.text: Tap Delete Account.
Confirm the deletion when prompted.

@graph.name: How to Remove Your iCloud Email
@graph.description: Remove your iCloud email from an iPhone by signing out of your Apple ID in the Settings app.

step.name: Open Settings
step.text: Open the Settings app on your iPhone.

itemListElement.text: Locate and tap the Settings app icon on your home screen.

step.name: Access Apple ID settings
step.text: Tap your name at the top of the Settings screen to open your Apple ID settings.

itemListElement.text: Tap your Apple ID banner at the top.

step.name: Sign out of iCloud
step.text: Scroll down and tap Sign Out to remove your iCloud email and other associated services from the device.

itemListElement.text: Scroll to the bottom of the Apple ID settings page.
Tap Sign Out and follow the prompts to confirm.

@graph.name: How to Sign Out from Gmail App on iPhone
@graph.description: Sign out from your Gmail account in the Gmail app on your iPhone by managing accounts directly within the app.

step.name: Open Gmail app
step.text: Open the Gmail app on your iPhone.

itemListElement.text: Locate the Gmail app icon on your home screen.
Tap to open it.

step.name: Access account settings
step.text: Tap your profile picture at the top of the screen to open the account menu.

itemListElement.text: Tap your profile icon in the top-right corner.

step.name: Manage accounts
step.text: Tap Manage Accounts on this device to open the account settings.

itemListElement.text: Select Manage Accounts on this device from the menu.

step.name: Sign out or remove account
step.text: Toggle off the account you want to sign out from, or tap Remove from this device to delete it completely.

itemListElement.text: Toggle off the desired Gmail account to sign out temporarily.
Tap Remove from this device to delete the account.

keyPoints.title: Temporarily Disable Mail on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: You can turn off the Mail feature for specific accounts to take a break from emails while keeping the account saved for other uses like Contacts or Calendars.

keyPoints.title: Log Out of Mail App
keyPoints.explanation: To fully remove an email account from your iPhone, go to Settings, select Mail, then Accounts, and delete the account, which removes it from the Mail app and other related apps.

keyPoints.title: Remove iCloud Email and Apple ID
keyPoints.explanation: To remove your iCloud email and Apple ID, you need to sign out from your Apple account in Settings, but be aware this disables iCloud services and device location features.

keyPoints.title: Sign Out from Gmail App
keyPoints.explanation: In the Gmail app, sign out by tapping your profile picture, choosing Manage Accounts, and toggling off or removing the account directly within the app.

keyPoints.title: Managing Email Sign-Out Tips

title.rendered: How to Use Invisible Ink in iMessage on iPhone and iPad?

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What It Is: Invisible Ink is an iMessage effect that hides your text or media until the recipient taps it.
  • How to Send: To send a message with Invisible Ink, long-press the blue send button and select the effect.
  • How to View: To view a received message, simply tap or swipe on the blurred bubble to temporarily reveal it.
  • Creative Uses: Use Invisible Ink to add fun and privacy to your chats with surprises, riddles, or spoilers.
  • Key Limitations: Invisible Ink only works in iMessage (blue bubbles) and requires the “Reduce Motion” setting to be disabled.

Apple’s Messages app is full of fun and interesting features designed to enhance your conversations. Among them, the Invisible Ink effect stands out. When enabled, this effect hides your message beneath a pixelated blur until the recipient taps it, adding a layer of mystery, surprise, or privacy.

In this post, you’ll learn how to use Invisible Ink in iMessage on your iPhone and iPad.

Table of Contents
  • What Is Invisible Ink and How Does It Work?
  • How to Send a Message with Invisible Ink on iPhone or iPad
  • How to View Invisible Ink Messages on iPhone
  • Tips and Tricks for Using Invisible Ink Creatively
  • Limitations to Keep in Mind
  • Troubleshooting: Invisible Ink Not Working?
  • Can Android Users See Invisible Ink Messages?
  • Ready to Add Some Mystery to Your Messages?

What Is Invisible Ink and How Does It Work?

Introduced in iOS 10, Invisible Ink is an iMessage bubble effect that adds a shimmering, pixelated blur over the text, emoji, or media you’re sharing. The recipient must tap or swipe over the blurred message to reveal its contents. Once viewed, the blur effect reappears automatically after a few seconds.

This feature is perfect for:

  • Sending surprises or spoilers without revealing too much upfront.
  • Keeping private content hidden from shoulder surfers.
  • Making conversations more interactive and playful.

How to Send a Message with Invisible Ink on iPhone or iPad

Sending a message with Invisible Ink is almost as simple as sending a regular iMessage, with just a couple of extra steps:

  1. Open the Messages app and start a new iMessage conversation or open an existing one.
  2. Type your message in the text box.
  3. To send an image or video, tap the + button, select Photos, and choose the media.
  4. Long-press the Send button (the upward blue arrow).
  5. Ensure you’re on the Bubble tab.
  6. Select Invisible Ink from the list of effects.
  7. Tap Send to deliver your message with the Invisible Ink effect.

That’s it! Your message will now appear blurred to the recipient until they interact with it.

How to View Invisible Ink Messages on iPhone

When you receive an Invisible Ink message, the notification will display:
“Message sent with Invisible Ink” instead of the usual preview.

To view the message:

  1. Tap the notification to open the conversation in Messages.
  2. You’ll see the message hidden under a shimmering, pixelated blur.
  3. Tap or swipe across the message to reveal it temporarily.
  4. After a few seconds, the blur effect will return automatically.

Tips and Tricks for Using Invisible Ink Creatively

Invisible Ink isn’t just about privacy; it adds creativity and excitement to your messages. Try using it in these fun and clever ways:

  • Hide surprises: Perfect for birthday messages, surprise party invites, or gift codes.
  • Play trivia or riddles: Send a question and hide the answer under Invisible Ink.
  • Send flirty or sweet notes: Make love notes or inside jokes feel more special.
  • Avoid spoilers: Hide plot reveals so your friend can choose when to see them.
  • Protect sensitive info: Share passwords, PINs, or private info securely.
  • Emoji/sticker fun: Send chains of emojis or stickers your friend reveals one by one.
  • Build suspense: Send a message or reply in Invisible Ink for a dramatic reveal.

Limitations to Keep in Mind

While fun and functional, Invisible Ink has some limitations tied to how iMessage works:

  • Only works with iMessage: The effect won’t appear if sent as an SMS or RCS message.
  • Can’t remove the effect after sending: Edit and Unsend do not remove the Invisible Ink effect.
  • Requires Motion Effects: If Reduce Motion is enabled, Invisible Ink (and other iMessage effects) won’t work.

Troubleshooting: Invisible Ink Not Working?

If Invisible Ink isn’t working or isn’t showing up for the recipient, here are a few steps you can take:

  • Ensure iMessage is enabled: Since the Invisible Ink effect is an iMessage-only feature, it won’t work if iMessage isn’t enabled on your iPhone. To check, go to Settings → Apps → Messages → iMessage and make sure it’s turned on.
  • Turn off Reduce Motion: Ensure Reduce Motion is turned off, as it disables message effects to conserve battery. Go to Settings → Accessibility → Motion.
  • Check your internet connection: iMessages require an active internet connection—Wi-Fi or cellular—to send effects.
  • Update iOS: Make sure both you and your recipient are running the latest iOS version to avoid compatibility issues.

Can Android Users See Invisible Ink Messages?

No. If you send an Invisible Ink message to someone using an Android device or an SMS message, it will appear as plain text or a regular image without any blur or animation. The effect is exclusive to iMessage on Apple devices.

Ready to Add Some Mystery to Your Messages?

Invisible Ink isn’t just a fun gimmick; it’s a privacy-focused feature that lets you control what your recipient sees and when they see it. Although it only takes a swipe or tap to reveal the message, the momentary suspense it creates adds a delightful twist to everyday conversations.

Have a favorite way to use Invisible Ink? Or did you run into any issues? Share your thoughts in the comments below, we’d love to hear from you!

FAQs

Can I use Invisible Ink in group chats?

Yes. It works the same way in group iMessage chats, and all participants using iMessage will be able to see the effect.

Why can’t I see the Invisible Ink effect?

You’re likely using SMS instead of iMessage, or Reduce Motion is turned on in your device settings.

Can I send Invisible Ink from a Mac?

Yes. You can send Invisible Ink messages from the Messages app on Mac, as long as your Mac is running macOS Sierra (10.12) or later.

Can I customize the Invisible Ink effect?

No. The Invisible Ink effect is not customizable—it comes in a standard shimmering blur.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I change country in the App Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple's stringent requirements make changing your App Store country harder to ensure a smooth transition and adherence to regional regulations. Each nation has its laws concerning digital media and applications. So, you must meet all the criteria to be able to continue purchasing items from your new country's App Store. Also, Apple doesn't want one to lose credit balance, subscriptions, pre-orders etc. This means that if even one condition is not satisfied, you can't complete the process. To learn more about this, go through what to do before changing your App Store Country or region.

mainEntity.name: How to change App Store country without a credit card?

acceptedAnswer.text: Changing your App Store country without a credit card is possible. When entering payment details, select 'None' as the payment method. This allows you to make the switch without entering a new card. However, you won't be able to make any purchases until you add a valid payment method. If you don't see the None option, maybe you have an unpaid balance or due payments. Also, recurring subscription mandates and Family Sharing prevent you from changing the App Store without a credit card. In such a case, you need to create a new Apple ID in that region.

mainEntity.name: How many times can I change my App Store country?

acceptedAnswer.text: There isn't a clear answer to how many times you can change your App Store country. However, to avoid issues, you should only change the App Store location when you really need to. Creating a new Apple ID with a new billing address can be a significantly better option if you need to change your App Store location frequently.

mainEntity.name: Does changing the App Store region affect any apps from the previous region?

acceptedAnswer.text: Changing the App Store region doesn't directly affect apps from the previous region. You can still use the app if it's already downloaded on your device. However, due to regional restrictions, you might not be able to make new purchases within the app or use all its features.

keyPoints.title: Invisible Ink Overview
keyPoints.explanation: Introduced in iOS 10, Invisible Ink is an iMessage feature that blurs messages, emojis, or media until the recipient taps or swipes to reveal, adding privacy and fun to your conversations.

keyPoints.title: How to Send Invisible Ink Messages
keyPoints.explanation: To send an Invisible Ink message, type a message, long-press the send button, select 'Invisible Ink,' and tap send; it works on iPhone and iPad with iOS 10 or later.

keyPoints.title: Viewing Invisible Ink Messages
keyPoints.explanation: When you receive an Invisible Ink message, it appears blurred, and you can reveal it by tapping or swiping across the message; it automatically re-blurs after a few seconds.

keyPoints.title: Creative Uses of Invisible Ink
keyPoints.explanation: Invisible Ink can be used for surprises, riddles, private info sharing, or building suspense, making conversations more playful and engaging.

keyPoints.title: Limitations & Troubleshooting
keyPoints.explanation: Invisible Ink only works with iMessage; it doesn't support SMS or Android, and requires disabled Reduce Motion settings and an active internet connection for proper functioning.

title.rendered: How to Close Apps on Apple Watch (watchOS 10 or Later)

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • When to Close Apps: Only close an Apple Watch app if it is frozen, slowing down your device, or draining battery.
  • How to Close Apps: Open the App Switcher with the side button (or Crown), then swipe left on an app to close it.
  • Why It’s Unnecessary: You don’t need to close apps; watchOS automatically suspends them to manage memory and save battery.
  • For a Smooth Watch: To keep your watch running smoothly, regularly restart it, update watchOS, and manage background app refresh.
  • Troubleshooting Apps: For a misbehaving app, try restarting your watch, updating watchOS, or reinstalling the specific app.

The Apple Watch is much more capable than the iPhone at managing apps efficiently in the background. However, there are times when you may want to close an app manually, whether it’s frozen, misbehaving, or draining your battery. Unlike the iPhone, though, there’s no simple swipe-up gesture to bring up the App Switcher on the Apple Watch.

This post details everything you need to know about closing apps on your Apple Watch.

Table of Contents
  • When Should You Close Apps on Apple Watch?
  • How to Close Apps on Apple Watch
    • Method 1: Using the Digital Crown or Side Button
    • Method 2: Force Quit a Frozen App
  • Can You Completely Quit Apps Like on iPhone?
  • Tips to Keep Your Apple Watch Running Smoothly
  • Troubleshooting Tips for Apple Watch Apps That Won't Open or Respond
    • 1. Restart your Apple Watch
    • 2. Update watchOS
    • 3. Delete and reinstall the problematic app
  • Video: How to Close Apple Watch Apps
  • Know It, Don’t Overdo It…

When Should You Close Apps on Apple Watch?

While you don’t need to manually close apps on your Apple Watch when they’re functioning normally, consider doing so if you notice any of the following issues:

  • An app freezes or crashes: If an app becomes unresponsive, closing and reopening it can resolve the problem.
  • The Apple Watch is slow or overheating: Sometimes, background processes can bog down your device. Closing apps may help restore normal function.
  • Battery is draining faster than usual: While not always the main culprit, troublesome apps can occasionally drain battery life more quickly than expected.

How to Close Apps on Apple Watch

If it’s just about restoring normal function or saving battery life, closing the app should suffice. However, if an app has become unresponsive, consider force-quitting it.

Method 1: Using the Digital Crown or Side Button

Depending on your watchOS version, the steps to close an app vary slightly. Let’s break it down:

For watchOS 10 or later:

  1. Press the Digital Crown twice to bring up the App Switcher.
  2. Use the Digital Crown or swipe up and down to scroll through your recent apps.
  3. Once you’ve located the app you want to close, swipe left on it and tap the ‘X’ button that appears.

For Older Versions of watchOS:

  1. Press the Side Button once to access the App Switcher.
  2. Scroll through apps, swipe left on the app to close it, and tap the ‘X’ button.

Method 2: Force Quit a Frozen App

If the app you’re currently using freezes and becomes unresponsive, you won’t be able to close it normally or access the App Switcher. In that case, force quitting the app is the last option. Here’s how:

  1. Open the problematic app.
  2. Press and hold the side button until the power-off screen appears.
  3. Release the Side button, then press and hold the Digital Crown until the app closes and you return to the watch face.
  4. If this fails, restart your Apple Watch.

Can You Completely Quit Apps Like on iPhone?

Yes, you can completely quit apps on Apple Watch like you do on iPhone, but the fact is, you don’t need to. Apple has designed watchOS to handle apps differently from iOS:

  • Unlike the iPhone, most apps on the Apple Watch automatically enter a suspended state when they haven’t been opened for a while. They don’t continue to run in the background, consuming battery and other resources.
  • Even the apps that need to deliver updated information every few minutes automatically refresh in short bursts as needed (like updating weather), but can’t run persistently in the background.
  • watchOS is optimized to handle background processes efficiently, so you generally won’t notice any performance improvement from manually closing apps for performance or battery reasons.

Tips to Keep Your Apple Watch Running Smoothly

While you already know that watchOS is capable of handling apps running in the background, you can still use these tips to ensure you don’t face any app-related issues:

  • Restart your Apple Watch regularly to clear temporary glitches.
  • Update to the latest version of watchOS for optimal performance and bug fixes.
  • Minimize the number of enabled complications and notifications.
  • Adjust the background app refresh setting in the Watch app on your iPhone to limit unnecessary updates.
  • Uninstall apps you rarely use.

Related: How to Use Apple Watch Always On Display

Troubleshooting Tips for Apple Watch Apps That Won’t Open or Respond

If closing or force-quitting an Apple Watch app does not resolve your issue, you can take a few additional steps.

1. Restart your Apple Watch 

Sometimes, restarting your Apple Watch can fix any technical glitches with apps. This closes all running apps on the Apple Watch and refreshes the background activities.

  1. Press and hold the side button until the shutdown screen appears.
  2. Tap the Power icon at the top right.
  3. Drag the Power Off slider.
  4. Wait a few seconds, then press and hold the side button again until you see the Apple logo.

If your Apple Watch doesn’t respond, press and hold the side button and the Digital Crown together until the Apple logo appears. It will force your Apple Watch to restart.

2. Update watchOS

It’s advisable to always run the latest version of watchOS on your Apple Watch to avoid system bugs.

You can update your Apple Watch by going to Settings → General → Software Update.

You can Download and Install an update if available.

3. Delete and reinstall the problematic app

If an app is having issues, it’s a good idea to delete and reinstall it. This usually fixes any problems and gives the app a fresh start.

  1. Press the Digital Crown to be on the Home Screen of your Apple Watch.
  2. Tap and hold an app icon until you see a small ‘x’ symbol appear above it.
  3. Tap the ‘x‘ and then select Delete App.

You can then go to the App Store and reinstall the app if you want to.

Video: How to Close Apple Watch Apps

Know It, Don’t Overdo It…

And that’s it; this is how you close apps on your Apple Watch. Though you don’t need to do it often, it’s a handy skill to know when an app misbehaves or freezes. Apple’s watchOS is excellent at managing resources, but force quitting specific apps can help you regain control quickly.

Still having trouble with a specific app? Drop a comment, and we’ll try to help you troubleshoot.

FAQs

Does closing apps save battery on Apple Watch?

Usually, no. Since watchOS suspends apps automatically, closing them rarely affects battery life unless one is misbehaving.

Can I close all apps at once?

No. You must close each app individually, either via the App Switcher or by force quitting it.

Why do apps keep running in the background?

Most apps do not continue running in the background. WatchOS suspends them automatically and only allows brief refreshes for essential updates.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I change country in the App Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple's stringent requirements make changing your App Store country harder to ensure a smooth transition and adherence to regional regulations. Each nation has its laws concerning digital media and applications. So, you must meet all the criteria to be able to continue purchasing items from your new country's App Store. Also, Apple doesn't want one to lose credit balance, subscriptions, pre-orders etc. This means that if even one condition is not satisfied, you can't complete the process. To learn more about this, go through what to do before changing your App Store Country or region.

mainEntity.name: How to change App Store country without a credit card?

acceptedAnswer.text: Changing your App Store country without a credit card is possible. When entering payment details, select 'None' as the payment method. If you don't see the None option, maybe you have an unpaid balance or due payments. @graph.description: Quickly close apps on your Apple Watch using the Digital Crown to free up resources and improve performance.

step.name: Open the App Switcher
step.text: Press the Digital Crown twice to bring up the App Switcher on your Apple Watch.

itemListElement.text: Press the Digital Crown two times quickly.

step.name: Find the app to close
step.text: Scroll through your recent apps using the Digital Crown or swipe up and down on the screen.

step.name: Close the app
step.text: Swipe left on the app you want to close, then tap the ‘X’ button to remove it from the App Switcher.

@graph.name: How to Force Quit a Frozen App on Apple Watch
@graph.description: Force quit a frozen or unresponsive app on your Apple Watch using the side button and Digital Crown.

step.text: Navigate to and open the app that is unresponsive.

itemListElement.text: Tap the problematic app on your Apple Watch to open it.

step.name: Bring up the power-off screen
step.text: Press and hold the side button until the power-off screen appears.

itemListElement.text: Locate the side button next to the Digital Crown.
Press and hold it until you see the power-off options.

step.name: Force quit the app
step.text: Release the side button, then press and hold the Digital Crown until the app closes and you return to the watch face.

itemListElement.text: Let go of the side button once the power-off screen is visible.

keyPoints.title: When Should You Close Apps on Apple Watch?
keyPoints.explanation: It's best to close apps only if they freeze, cause overheating, slow down your device, or drain the battery unusually, rather than regularly closing apps not in use.

keyPoints.title: How to Close Apps on Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: You can close apps using the Digital Crown or Side Button, depending on your watchOS version, and force quit frozen apps when necessary for quick troubleshooting.

keyPoints.title: Can You Completely Quit Apps Like on iPhone?
keyPoints.explanation: Most apps on Apple Watch automatically suspend when not in use, so manually quitting isn't necessary; watchOS is designed to handle apps efficiently in the background.

keyPoints.title: Tips to Keep Your Apple Watch Running Smoothly
keyPoints.explanation: Regularly restart your device, keep watchOS updated, limit notifications, manage background refresh, and uninstall rarely used apps to maintain optimal performance.

keyPoints.title: Troubleshooting Tips for Apple Watch Apps That Won't Open or Respond
keyPoints.explanation: If apps misbehave, restart your Watch, update watchOS, or delete and reinstall problematic apps to resolve issues and restore proper function.

title.rendered: Adaptive Power in iOS 26: The Smart Way to Save Battery on iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Adaptive Power in iOS 26 works quietly in the background to reduce battery drain by making smart, subtle adjustments during high power use.
  • It’s only available on newer models like iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16 lineup, and requires iOS 26 with Apple Intelligence enabled.
  • You can enable it manually in Settings under Battery > Power Mode, where it runs automatically without changing how your iPhone feels.
  • It’s different from Low Power Mode, which activates at 20% and cuts more aggressively; Adaptive Power is less noticeable and kicks in earlier.
  • This feature hints at future battery strategies for slimmer iPhones, balancing performance and battery life without needing frequent user input.

When your iPhone’s battery gets low, you probably dim the screen, close some apps, or turn on Low Power Mode. But with iOS 26, Apple is flipping that idea. Instead of you having to adjust to save power, your iPhone will now do it for you.

It’s introducing a new feature called Adaptive Power. Here’s what Adaptive Power is, what it does, and how you can turn it on.

What Is Adaptive Power in iOS 26?

It’s like a smarter, lighter version of Low Power Mode. It quietly monitors how you use your phone and makes small performance adjustments when it detects unusually high power consumption. It’s not aggressive or annoying. You might not even notice it. But it works behind the scenes to stretch your battery just a bit more when you need it most.

Here’s what Adaptive Power actually does:

  • If you’re recording video or editing photos, things that drain power quickly, your iPhone might slightly lower the screen brightness or slow down background processes.
  • Some apps may take a fraction longer to launch or load.
  • The idea is to save small amounts of energy in the moment, so you go longer before needing a charge.

This isn’t like Low Power Mode, which kicks in at 20% and aggressively shuts down background activity. Adaptive Power is more of a precision tool, a scalpel, not a hammer. It steps in only when needed and makes sure your iPhone doesn’t waste power where it doesn’t have to.

To give you more control, Apple has also added an Adaptive Power Notifications toggle. It notifies you when your iPhone automatically slows performance to save power. So if you notice a dip in performance, you’ll now know what’s causing it. 

Which iPhones Support Adaptive Power?

Now, here’s the catch: Adaptive Power requires Apple Intelligence, Apple’s new on-device AI system. That means it only works on iPhones that support Apple Intelligence.

So far, the feature is available on:

  • iPhone 15 Pro
  • iPhone 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16, 16 Plus
  • iPhone 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16e
  • iPhone 17
  • iPhone Air
  • iPhone 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max

So, if you’re using anything older than an iPhone 15 Pro, even if you install iOS 26, you won’t see Adaptive Power in your settings.

Related: How to Get the iOS 26 Developer Beta on Your iPhone

How to Turn On Adaptive Power in iOS 26

The feature is turned off by default. If you want to enable it, you can head to:

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Scroll down and tap Battery.
  3. Tap Power Mode.
  4. Toggle on Adaptive Power to enable it.

Once turned on, it starts working silently in the background. You may not notice a big change in performance, but your battery might last just long enough to reach a charger. You can also enable notifications from the same Settings page.

Why Adaptive Power Matters for the Future

With iOS 26 now fully rolled out, Adaptive Power is confirmed to be part of Apple’s broader strategy to make the iPhone more power‑smart without requiring you to change your habits. It quietly balances performance and efficiency, stepping in when needed to extend battery life in real‑world use.

It also points toward the future. With devices like the iPhone 17 Air focusing on being thinner and lighter with smaller batteries, features like Adaptive Power are crucial to maintaining good battery performance without compromise.

So, if you’ve ever found yourself stuck with 5% battery and no charger in sight, this feature is the quiet little upgrade you can now count on.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I change country in the App Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple's stringent requirements make changing your App Store country harder to ensure a smooth transition and adherence to regional regulations. Each nation has its laws concerning digital media and applications. So, you must meet all the criteria to be able to continue purchasing items from your new country's App Store. Also, Apple doesn't want one to lose credit balance, subscriptions, pre-orders etc. This means that if even one condition is not satisfied, you can't complete the process. To learn more about this, go through what to do before changing your App Store Country or region.

mainEntity.name: How to change App Store country without a credit card?

acceptedAnswer.text: Changing your App Store country without a credit card is possible. When entering payment details, select 'None' as the payment method. If you don't see the None option, maybe you have an unpaid balance or due payments. keyPoints.title: What Is Adaptive Power in iOS 26?
keyPoints.explanation: Adaptive Power is a smarter, less noticeable version of Low Power Mode that optimizes your iPhone's performance by monitoring usage and making small efficiency adjustments when high power consumption is detected.

keyPoints.title: Supported iPhone Models for Adaptive Power
keyPoints.explanation: Adaptive Power is available only on newer iPhones supporting Apple Intelligence, including iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16 series, and iPhone 16e, and requires iOS 26.

keyPoints.title: How to Enable Adaptive Power in iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: To turn on Adaptive Power, go to Settings, then Battery, tap Power Mode, and toggle it on—once enabled, it works automatically in the background to conserve battery.

keyPoints.title: Difference from Low Power Mode
keyPoints.explanation: Unlike Low Power Mode, which activates at 20% and aggressively limits background activity, Adaptive Power makes small, targeted adjustments only when necessary, helping extend battery life subtly.

keyPoints.title: Future Implications of Adaptive Power**
keyPoints.explanation: Adaptive Power is an early step toward more intelligent battery management that could be especially useful for future ultra-thin iPhones with smaller batteries, ensuring sustained performance without user intervention.

title.rendered: iPhone Fold – Everything We Know So Far

content.rendered:
Apple hasn’t launched a completely new iPhone form factor in years. But in 2026, that could change. The long-rumored foldable iPhone, sometimes called the iPhone Fold or iPhone Flip is finally seems closer than ever. After years of patents, prototypes, and delayed timelines, multiple credible sources now point to a late 2026 debut. And if leaks are anything to go by, this might be Apple’s most ambitious iPhone yet.

In this article, we’ll walk through everything we know about the foldable iPhone so far, from the design and display sizes to the release date and expected pricing.

Note: Apple has not officially announced the foldable iPhone. All details below are based on reliable leaks and analyst reports.

Quick Overview of the Foldable iPhone

Here’s a snapshot of what rumors and leaks consistently suggest about Apple’s first foldable:

Design: Crease-Free and Thinner than iPhone 17 Air

Apple is working on a foldable iPhone that opens like a book, similar to the Galaxy Z Fold. On the outside, it works just like any other iPhone with a full display. Unfold it, and you get a 7.8‑inch screen that’s almost the size of an iPad mini, but small enough to slip into your pocket. Apple is also rumored to be targeting a crease‑free design, which could set it apart from most foldable phones on the market.

The hinge is rumored to be made from Liquid Metal for extra strength, with leaks pointing to a thickness of around 9.2mm when folded and just under 4.8mm when unfolded. That would make it thinner than the iPhone 17 Air and on par with current foldables.

Another interesting change could be in the biometrics. Several leaks suggest Apple might skip Face ID on the Fold and go with Touch ID built into the side button instead.

Display: A 7.8-inch iPad Mini in Your Pocket

The iPhone Fold is expected to have two OLED displays. The outer screen will be around 5.5 inches, giving you a compact iPhone experience when the phone is folded. The main display on the inside opens up to roughly 7.8 inches, big enough to feel like a small iPad.

Apple is said to be using custom Samsung panels designed to avoid the deep crease seen on most foldables. The inner display will reportedly also feature an under‑display camera to keep the viewing area clean, while the outer screen could use a small hole‑punch camera.

Both screens are expected to support high refresh rates for smooth scrolling, animations, and gaming, along with brightness levels on par with Apple’s Pro models.

Camera: Pro-Level Lenses, But No Telephoto

The iPhone Fold is expected to feature a dual-camera setup on the back, using the same 48MP main and ultra-wide lenses found in the iPhone 16 Pro. Image quality should closely match Apple’s Pro lineup, though the Fold will reportedly skip the telephoto lens.

For selfies and video calls, the outer display is rumored to include a hole-punch camera, while the inner foldable screen will use a 24MP under-display camera, Apple’s first implementation of this tech. This design keeps the main display completely unobstructed, offering a cleaner experience for watching videos and gaming.

Performance: On par with iPhone 18 Pro

Launching alongside the iPhone 18 lineup means the Fold should ship with Apple’s next‑generation A20 Pro chip built on TSMC’s 2nm process. Some leaks suggest it could get the A21 Pro chip the following year, but that’s less certain. What is certain is that Apple will opt for Pro‑level hardware to handle the demands of dual displays. RAM will likely be integrated into the chip package for better efficiency.

The iPhone 17 Pro is rumored to feature a vapor chamber to help keep temperatures in check. It wouldn’t be surprising if the Fold gets a similar cooling system, but given its slim design, these details remain speculative for now.

On the software side, iOS 27 will be optimized for foldables, with features designed to leverage the larger inner display. This mix of optimized hardware and software suggests the first‑generation Fold should deliver smooth performance, even if the finer details are still a mystery.

Battery: Dual-Cell Setup, Just like Most Foldables

Battery details remain vague, but early leaks suggest a dual‑cell setup, common in foldables, which allows the phone to charge faster and distribute power evenly across both halves of the device. However, exact capacity numbers haven’t surfaced yet.

Charging speeds are also still a mystery. Apple has been conservative here, so it’s safe to expect something in line with current Pro models. Wireless charging and MagSafe support are likely to carry over, but we’ll have to wait for more solid details.

Colors: Expect a Pro‑Style Palette

No concrete leaks on colors yet. Normally, color options do not leak until closer to launch.

However, we can expect the Fold series to have a similar palette to that of the iPhone Pro series. Muted colors like Space Black, White, and Natural Titanium are likely. Apple could also introduce one bold color to make the Fold stand out, similar to the Orange seen in iPhone 17 Pro leaks.

Connectivity: A Pro Series Phone in Disguise

Connectivity should match the iPhone 18 Pro. Expect 5G with either the latest Qualcomm or Apple modem, Wi‑Fi 7 for faster speeds, and Bluetooth 5.4 for improved stability with accessories.

USB‑C will remain, and with the Fold positioned as a premium device, it will likely support USB 3 speeds like the Pro models.

Satellite connectivity for Emergency SOS and Roadside Assistance is also expected. For now, these are all based on speculation, as nothing major has leaked about the Fold’s connectivity.

iPhone Fold’s Expected Pricing and Release Date

The iPhone Fold is expected to launch in September 2026 alongside the iPhone 18 lineup. Analysts like Ming‑Chi Kuo and Mark Gurman point to a fall release, in line with Apple’s usual flagship cycle.

Pricing will likely start around $1,999, with estimates ranging from $1,800 to $2,300. While expensive compared to Pro models, it’s competitive with other premium foldables. Exact launch details will become clearer closer to 2026.

Here’s a Timeline of iPhone Fold Leaks Happened So Far

This timeline provides a clear view of how leaks have evolved over time. These leaks are listed in reverse-chronological (descending) order, with the newest at the top and older ones at the bottom.

Note: These leaks can sometimes contain contradictory information, as different sources claim different things. We can only be certain once the device is officially released to the public.

Foldable iPhone to Feature Breakthrough 24MP Under-Display Camera

November 10, 2025

JP Morgan reported that Apple’s foldable iPhone will feature a 24-megapixel under-display camera, the first of its kind in the industry. The ultra-thin device, described by Mark Gurman as “two titanium iPhone Airs side-by-side,” will also include two 48MP rear cameras and Touch ID in the side button, though LiDAR and optical stabilization may be omitted.

iPhone Fold to Feature 24MP Under-Display Camera

November 7, 2025

JP Morgan reported that Apple’s first foldable iPhone will include a 24-megapixel under-screen camera on the inner display, the highest resolution yet for this technology. The camera uses six plastic lens elements, marking a major leap in image clarity. However, the report notes the device may omit LiDAR and optical stabilization to maintain a slimmer design.

Apple Stockpiling Parts for Foldable iPhone Ahead of 2026 Launch

October 31, 2025

Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital reported that Apple is stockpiling key components, including foldable OLED panels, titanium frames, and advanced hinges, for its first foldable iPhone. The device is entering pre-production and is expected to launch in September 2026 as part of the iPhone 18 lineup.

Foldable iPhone Launch May Slip to 2027

October 17, 2025

Japan’s Mizuho Securities reported that Apple’s first foldable iPhone could be delayed to 2027 as design decisions, including the hinge mechanism, are still being finalized. The device is expected to feature a 7.58-inch inner display and 5.38-inch outer screen, with production estimates reduced from 13 million to nine million units.

Foldable iPhone May Cost Less to Produce

October 13, 2025

Ming-Chi Kuo reported that Apple’s foldable iPhone hinge will cost around $70–$80 per unit—lower than earlier estimates of $100–$120. The drop comes from optimized assembly design and Foxconn’s joint venture with hinge maker Shin Zu Shing, potentially allowing Apple to improve margins or offer a lower launch price.

Foldable iPhone to Feature Titanium and Aluminum Frame

October 8, 2025

Jeff Pu reported that Apple’s 2026 foldable iPhone will use a titanium-aluminum frame, expanding the company’s use of premium metals. The device is expected to be around 4.5mm thick when unfolded, featuring a titanium body for strength and aluminum components to reduce weight.

Samsung to Supply Foldable Displays for Apple

September 29, 2025

Samsung Display president Lee Cheong confirmed plans to produce foldable OLED panels for a major American company, widely believed to be Apple. The displays are expected to power Apple’s first foldable iPhone, set for a 2026 release with a crease-free design, Touch ID, and the A20 chip.

Foldable iPhone Design Compared to Two iPhone Airs Joined at the Hinge

September 22, 2025

Mark Gurman described Apple’s 2026 foldable iPhone as resembling “two titanium iPhone Airs side-by-side,” featuring an ultra-thin body and book-style design. The titanium device will likely cost around $2,000 and include a 7.8-inch inner screen, 5.5-inch outer display, dual rear cameras, and side-button Touch ID.

Foldable iPhone Coming in 2026, Foldable iPad to Follow in 2028

September 2, 2025

Ming-Chi Kuo reported that Apple plans to launch its first foldable iPhone in 2026 as part of the iPhone 18 lineup, followed by a foldable iPad in 2028. Both devices will use ultra-thin cover glass supplied by Corning, with GIS handling finishing and assembly.

Foldable iPhone to Use Side-Button Touch ID, Not Under-Screen Sensor

September 1, 2025

Ming-Chi Kuo reaffirmed that Apple’s 2026 foldable iPhone will feature Touch ID integrated into the side button, dismissing rumors of an under-display fingerprint sensor. He expects Luxshare ICT to supply the Touch ID module and predicts a book-style design with a 7.8-inch inner and 5.5-inch outer display.

Foldable iPhone to Include Four Cameras and Touch ID

August 24, 2025

Mark Gurman reported that Apple’s first foldable iPhone will feature four cameras, a Touch ID power button instead of Face ID, and a book-style design. The device will use Apple’s second-generation C2 modem, omit a SIM slot, and is expected to launch in 2026.

Apple’s 18.8-Inch Foldable Device Delayed Beyond 2026

August 4, 2025

Analyst Jeff Pu reported that Apple’s larger 18.8-inch foldable, initially planned for late 2026 production, has been postponed, likely to 2027. He still expects the smaller foldable iPhone to stay on track for a second-half 2026 launch.

JPMorgan: Foldable iPhone Tipped for September 2026 Launch

July 29, 2025

JPMorgan expects Apple’s first foldable iPhone to debut in September 2026 with the iPhone 18 lineup. Priced around $1,999, it’s rumored to feature a crease‑free 7.8‑inch inner display, 5.5‑inch outer screen, titanium chassis, and Touch ID.

Foldable iPhone’s Display Sizes Leaked

July 22, 2025

TrendForce claims Apple’s first foldable iPhone will feature a 7.8‑inch inner display and a 5.5‑inch outer display. Launch is expected in the second half of 2026, with a crease‑free design and Touch ID power button.

iOS 27 to Focus on Foldable iPhone Features

July 21, 2025

Mark Gurman reports that iOS 27 will prioritize software tailored for Apple’s first foldable iPhone, expected in late 2026. The book‑style device will feature a 7.8‑inch inner screen, a 5.5‑inch outer display, a titanium hinge, and Touch ID in the side button. Regular iPhones will still see UI updates next year.

Foldable iPhone Price and Thickness Leak

July 16, 2025

UBS analysts expect Apple’s foldable iPhone to start between $1,800 and $2,000, making it the most expensive iPhone yet. On Weibo, Instant Digital claims it will measure around 4.8mm when unfolded; it’s slightly thicker than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 7. The device is still on track for a 2026 launch.

Foldable iPhone to Feature ‘Crease-Free’ Display

July 15, 2025

Ming-Chi Kuo says Samsung Display will supply Apple with a custom “crease‑free” OLED panel for its foldable iPhone, using metal plates from Fine M‑Tec to manage stress during bending. The device is expected in late 2026 with a 7.8‑inch inner screen, a 5.5‑inch outer display, and a Touch ID side button.

Foldable iPhone Display Production Underway

July 9, 2025

ETNews reports that Samsung Display has begun producing OLED panels for Apple’s first foldable iPhone at its A3 factory in Korea. The device is expected in 2026 with a 7‑inch crease‑free screen, a titanium hinge, and a Touch ID side button, priced over $2,000.

Foldable iPhone Development Moves to Prototyping Phase

July 2, 2025

DigiTimes reports Apple’s foldable iPhone has entered the P1 prototyping stage with suppliers. It’s expected to complete testing by late 2025 and launch alongside the iPhone 18 lineup in fall 2026. Work on a foldable iPad is reportedly paused.

Foldable iPhone Leak Points to Dual 48MP Rear Cameras

June 26, 2025

Digital Chat Station claims Apple’s foldable iPhone will feature dual 48MP rear cameras, matching the iPhone 16 Pro’s main and ultra‑wide setup. The device is also expected to use a crease‑free hinge and a Touch ID-equipped side button, and to feature under‑screen and hole‑punch front cameras for different modes.

Foldable iPhone Production to Begin This Fall for 2026 Launch

June 18, 2025

Ming-Chi Kuo says Foxconn will start producing Apple’s foldable iPhone by late September or October. Launching in fall 2026, it’s expected to feature a 5.5‑inch outer screen, 7.8‑inch inner display, near‑invisible crease, and Touch ID in the power button.

iPhone 18 Fold Launching Next Year With Two Key Advantages

June 4, 2025

Mark Gurman says Apple’s foldable iPhone will debut in 2026 with a nearly invisible crease and a high‑quality hinge. It’s expected to feature a 7.8‑inch inner display, 5.5‑inch outer screen, Touch ID in the power button, and a thinner titanium‑steel frame.

iPhone 18 Pro and Fold to Feature A20 Chip on 2nm Process

June 3, 2025

Jeff Pu says the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max, and Fold will use Apple’s new A20 chip built on TSMC’s 2nm process. It’s expected to be faster, more power‑efficient, and use advanced packaging that integrates RAM for better performance, battery life, and thermal management.

Foldable iPhone Outer Display to Feature Hole‑Punch Camera

May 15, 2025

Digital Chat Station claims Apple’s foldable iPhone will have a hole‑punch camera on its 5.5‑inch outer screen, while the 7.8‑inch inner display uses an under‑screen camera. Touch ID is said to be integrated into the side button.

Gurman: Foldable iPhone Expected by 2027

May 12, 2025

Mark Gurman says Apple’s first foldable iPhone should debut in late 2026, with most sales happening in 2027. It’s expected to have a nearly invisible crease, book‑style design, and a price of around $2,000.

Apple’s Second Foldable iPhone Set for 2027 Launch, Claims Kuo

May 5, 2025

Ming-Chi Kuo says Apple’s second foldable iPhone will arrive in late 2027, following the first-gen model expected in 2026. The second version could launch alongside a redesigned Pro model for the iPhone’s 20th anniversary.

Foldable iPhone Said to Have Two Key Advantages

May 5, 2025

Mark Gurman reports that Apple’s foldable iPhone will aim for two standout features: a nearly invisible crease for a smooth 7.8–8-inch inner display and a high-quality hinge made of titanium and stainless steel. The goal is to deliver a more seamless look and feel compared to current foldables.

Pro & Foldable iPhones Coming in Fall, Standard in Spring

May 3, 2025

According to The Information, Apple will shift its release cycle in 2026. Pro and foldable models will launch in the fall, while standard iPhones will move to spring 2027 to streamline production.

iPhone Fold Camera Leak Confirms Outer Display Setup

April 16, 2025

Apple’s foldable iPhone will have a dual-lens rear camera, an under-screen camera for the main display, and a hole‑punch camera on the outer screen, according to yeux1122. The book‑style device, expected late 2026, will use Touch ID in the side button instead of Face ID to save space. Price is rumored to be $2,000–$2,300.

iPhone Fold Under‑Screen Camera Won’t Support Face ID

April 15, 2025

Apple’s foldable iPhone will use an under‑screen selfie camera on the main display, but it won’t include Face ID hardware, says Digital Chat Station. Instead, the phone is expected to rely on Touch ID in the side button to save internal space, a move also backed by analyst Ming‑Chi Kuo. The first‑gen model is set to launch late 2026 at around $2,000.

Foldable iPhone to Use Samsung OLED Panels Exclusively

April 15, 2025

Apple’s first foldable iPhone will rely solely on Samsung Display for its OLED panels, reports Business Korea. Apple skipped LG Display and BOE, citing Samsung’s lead in reducing screen creases. The device, expected late next year, will feature a 5.5-inch outer and 7.8-inch inner display, both nearly crease-free. Supply could surpass 15 million units annually.

Foldable iPhone Expected to Cost $2,100–$2,300, Exceeding Samsung’s Price

April 15, 2025

Weibo leaker Instant Digital claims Apple’s foldable iPhone will start at $2,100-$2,300, roughly $200–$400 more than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold6. This makes it about $1,000 pricier than the current iPhone 16 Pro Max.

Foldable iPhone Screens Leak With Under-Screen and Punch-Hole Cameras

April 14, 2025

Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station reveals the foldable iPhone’s 7.76-inch inner display will have a 2713×1920 resolution with under-screen camera tech, while the 5.49-inch outer screen uses 2088×1422 resolution with a punch-hole camera. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo confirms these sizes and calls the inner screen crease-free.

iPhone Fold to Feature iPad-Style 4:3 Aspect Ratio, Says Chinese Leaker

March 28, 2025

Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station revealed Apple’s foldable iPhone will have a 4:3 aspect ratio on the inner display, matching iPad models for better software compatibility and multitasking. This aligns with analyst Ming-Chi Kuo’s earlier confirmation of a 7.8-inch crease-free inner screen and a 5.5-inch outer screen.

iPhone Fold to Use Metallic Glass Hinge for Durability and Crease Reduction

March 27, 2025

Weibo leaker Instant Digital revealed Apple will use metallic glass, a super-strong, corrosion-resistant amorphous metal, for the hinge of its foldable iPhone. This 2.5x harder-than-titanium material aims to improve hinge durability and reduce screen creasing for the “iPhone Fold.”

Gurman: Foldable iPhone Expected in 2026 With $2,000 Price Tag

March 24, 2025

Mark Gurman, in his Power On newsletter for Bloomberg, says Apple’s first foldable iPhone is on track for a 2026 launch with a starting price around $2,000. The book-style device has reportedly entered the New Product Introduction phase at Foxconn, with mass production planned for late 2026.

Kuo: Foldable iPhone to Use Liquid Metal Hinges for Durability

March 21, 2025

Ming-Chi Kuo says Apple will use liquid metal hinges in its foldable iPhone to improve durability and reduce screen creasing. Dongguan EonTec will be the exclusive supplier. The device is expected to launch in late 2026 with a book-style design.

Foldable iPhone to Prioritize Battery Life Despite Slim Design

March 21, 2025

According to Korean news aggregator yeux1122 on Naver, Apple is optimizing the display driver IC and other components to boost battery life while keeping the foldable iPhone thin.

Apple Improves Foldable Display Efficiency by Shrinking Driver IC

March 18, 2025

Weibo leaker Phone Chip Expert reports Apple has reduced the foldable display driver IC from 28nm to 16nm, boosting power efficiency and helping extend battery life in the upcoming foldable iPhone.

Foldable iPhone to Borrow Tech from iPhone 17 Air, Says Gurman

March 17, 2025

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports Apple’s upcoming foldable iPhone will use technology from the ultra-thin iPhone 17 Air, including display, battery, modem, and chip advancements. The device, expected in late 2026 or early 2027, aims for a book-style fold with a nearly crease-free screen, leveraging Apple’s latest innovations for performance and efficiency.

Kuo: Foldable iPhone to Launch Late 2026 With Book-Style Design

March 5, 2025

Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo predicts Apple’s first foldable iPhone will debut in late 2026 or early 2027 with a book-style design. It’s expected to feature a 7.8-inch crease-free inner display, a 5.5-inch cover display, a titanium build, Touch ID on the side button, and a price tag starting above $2,000.

Apple’s 2026 Foldable iPhone Reportedly Crease-Free

February 25, 2025

ETNews reports Apple has nearly eliminated the display crease in its upcoming foldable iPhone, a breakthrough achieved with new materials. Supplier selection is set to wrap by April, with mass component production expected in the second half of 2025. Samsung Display will provide the OLED panels, Corning will provide the ultra-thin glass, and Amphenol will provide the hinge.

Alleged Display Sizes Leak for Foldable iPhone

February 21, 2025

Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station claims Apple’s foldable iPhone will feature a 5.49-inch outer screen (shorter and wider than Oppo’s Find N5) and a 7.74-inch inner display that unfolds like an iPad. Both are said to use “unprecedented aspect ratios.”

Apple Locks in Ultra-Thin Glass Supplier for Foldable iPhone

February 12, 2025

According to The Elec (via DigiTimes), Apple has tapped Lens Technology as the primary supplier of ultra-thin glass for its first foldable device. Production is set to ramp up in 2025, ahead of a rumored launch in late 2026. The UTG will feature a thinned central section for added durability.

Apple Nearing Final Choice of Supplier for Foldable iPhone Display

January 31, 2025

A report from Naver’s yeux1122 claims Apple is close to selecting a supplier for its foldable display, with a decision expected by April. The company is enforcing strict standards for thickness, durability, and crease prevention, signaling steady progress toward a foldable iPhone, potentially launching between 2026 and 2027.

Kuo: Foldable iPhone Still in Planning Stage, Timeline Unclear

January 10, 2025

Ming-Chi Kuo clarified that Apple’s foldable iPhone is still in the planning phase, despite earlier translations suggesting 2025 mass production. While the device could debut in late 2025 or 2026, its future hinges on design readiness and market considerations, and eSIM-only support could pose regional challenges.

Analyst: Apple’s 2026 Foldable iPhone Could Revive Declining Market

December 2, 2024

Display analyst Ross Young predicts Apple will debut its first foldable iPhone in late 2026, potentially sparking renewed interest in foldables. Expected to feature a 7.9–8.3-inch clamshell design, the device could boost the stagnating foldable market, with forecasts pointing to record growth when it launches.

Foldable iPhone Reportedly Adopting Clamshell Design Like Galaxy Z Flip

July 23, 2024

The Information reports Apple is developing a clamshell-style foldable iPhone, internally codenamed “V68,” targeting a 2026 launch. Similar to Samsung’s Galaxy Z Flip, the device faces challenges with crease removal, but supplier discussions suggest the project is moving forward.

Foldable iPhone Expected No Earlier Than 2027

June 3, 2024

TrendForce reports Apple is unlikely to release a foldable iPhone before 2027 as it continues to refine crease-free screens and durability. While late to the market, analysts believe Apple’s eventual entry could disrupt the foldable segment thanks to its strong brand and customer base.

Analyst Predicts Foldable iPhone Mass Production in 2026

May 6, 2024

Haitong analyst Jeff Pu claims Apple’s first foldable iPhone, with a 7.9–8.3 inch display, is set for mass production in late 2026. It will reportedly follow a larger 20.3-inch foldable iPad or MacBook, arriving in 2025, marking Apple’s entry into foldable devices through its high-end iPhone line.

iPhone Fold Pushed to 2027 Amid Durability and Design Challenges

March 28, 2024

Reports from Alpha Biz and The Information suggest Apple has delayed the foldable iPhone to early 2027 due to supply issues and technical hurdles. Two clamshell-style prototypes are in testing, but concerns over screen creases, hinge design, and display durability have raised doubts about whether the project will move forward on schedule.

Foldable iPhone Reportedly Paused After Samsung Panels Fail Testing

February 16, 2024

A rumor from Fixed Focus Digital claims Apple has suspended foldable iPhone development after Samsung’s latest folding displays failed internal stress tests and broke down within days. The project will remain on hold until a panel meets Apple’s durability standards, though work on a foldable iPad appears unaffected.

Apple Testing Two Foldable iPhone Prototypes, Earliest Launch in 2026

February 7, 2024

According to The Information, Apple is developing two clamshell-style foldable iPhone prototypes but hasn’t committed them to mass production. 2026 is the earliest possible launch, though the project could be scrapped if durability, hinge design, or feature set fails to meet Apple’s high standards.

Apple’s First Foldable Could Arrive in 2026, May Replace iPad Mini

February 2, 2024

A report from The Elec suggested Apple is targeting a 2026–2027 launch for its first foldable device, possibly a 7–8 inch model positioned to replace the iPad mini. Samsung and LG have been sending panel samples, but Apple is still finalizing specs and debating whether it will debut a foldable iPhone or iPad.

Samsung Display Restructures Team to Focus on Apple’s Foldable Panels

December 11, 2023

According to The Elec, Samsung Display has reorganized its Apple division to streamline the development of foldable panels. Leveraging experience from its own foldable devices, Samsung is working alongside LG Display on panels that could be used in Apple’s future foldable iPhones, with the earliest launch expectations still set for 2025 or later.

Apple Orders Large Batch of Samsung Foldable Displays for Testing

September 10, 2020

Leaker Ice Universe claimed Apple requested a “large number” of foldable phone display samples from Samsung for a year-long testing phase. The move suggested Apple was ramping up foldable iPhone development, building on earlier trials of Samsung’s flexible OLED technology.

Apple Teams Up With LG Display for Foldable iPhone Development

October 11, 2017

A Korean report claims Apple is working with LG Display on a foldable iPhone, avoiding Samsung due to concerns over tech leaks. LG has prototypes that fold like a book or roll like a scroll, and a dedicated team is reportedly developing a foldable OLED panel for Apple. Mass production isn’t expected until at least 2020.

LG Reportedly Supplying Foldable Displays for Future iPhones

December 16, 2016

A report from ETNews claimed LG would start mass-producing foldable OLED displays in 2018, with Apple among the companies set to receive them. While early prototypes showed book-like and rollable designs, the rumor suggested Apple was still exploring multiple iPhone concepts, including foldable options supported by its own patents.

That’s all we know for now. Will have to wait until fall 2026 for the iPhone Fold to launch to confirm any of these details. We’ll keep this page updated with the latest info, so stay tuned.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I change country in the App Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple's stringent requirements make changing your App Store country harder to ensure a smooth transition and adherence to regional regulations. Each nation has its laws concerning digital media and applications. So, you must meet all the criteria to be able to continue purchasing items from your new country's App Store. Also, Apple doesn't want one to lose credit balance, subscriptions, pre-orders etc. This means that if even one condition is not satisfied, you can't complete the process. To learn more about this, go through what to do before changing your App Store Country or region.

mainEntity.name: How to change App Store country without a credit card?

acceptedAnswer.text: Changing your App Store country without a credit card is possible. When entering payment details, select 'None' as the payment method. This allows you to make the switch without entering a new card. However, you won't be able to make any purchases until you add a valid payment method. If you don't see the None option, maybe you have an unpaid balance or due payments. Also, recurring subscription mandates and Family Sharing prevent you from changing the App Store without a credit card. In such a case, you need to create a new Apple ID in that region.

mainEntity.name: How many times can I change my App Store country?

acceptedAnswer.text: There isn't a clear answer to how many times you can change your App Store country. However, to avoid issues, you should only change the App Store location when you really need to. Creating a new Apple ID with a new billing address can be a significantly better option if you need to change your App Store location frequently.

mainEntity.name: Does changing the App Store region affect any apps from the previous region?

acceptedAnswer.text: Changing the App Store region doesn't directly affect apps from the previous region. You can still use the app if it's already downloaded on your device. However, due to regional restrictions, you might not be able to make new purchases within the app or use all its features.

acceptedAnswer.text: Make sure Dolby Atmos is turned on by heading to Settings > Apps > Music. Also, ensure you're using compatible headphones and that you're playing a track labeled with the Dolby Atmos badge.

mainEntity.name: Is Dolby Atmos better than Lossless on Apple Music?

acceptedAnswer.text: They're different. Dolby Atmos gives you a 3D surround effect, while Lossless delivers higher sound quality. If your device and headphones support both, you can use both together.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can still see old messages after turning off DMs. Blocking, restricting, or limiting who can message you only affects new incoming messages.

mainEntity.name: Can I limit DMs without going private?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can block message requests from strangers and followers while keeping your profile public.

mainEntity.name: Is there a way to auto-delete DMs?

title.rendered: What Is Apple Universal Control & How to Use It (Mac and iPad)

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Universal Control links Mac and iPad seamlessly so you can use one keyboard and mouse across both devices for typing, drag-and-drop, and gestures.
  • Requires updated OS and same Apple ID with two-factor authentication, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and Handoff active; works best within 30 feet.
  • Enable it under System Settings on Mac via Displays > Advanced, and on iPad via Settings > General > AirPlay & Continuity > Cursor and Keyboard.
  • Use it by moving the pointer to screen edges—the cursor snaps over to the next device, letting you control it instantly without setup every time.
  • Some VPNs or old OS versions can block it, so update software, check connections, and disable any interfering network tools for smoother use.

Ever wanted to use the same mouse and keyboard on both your Mac and iPad without dealing with wires or juggling extra apps? That’s exactly what Universal Control lets you do. I’ll walk you through how I set it up, how it actually works day to day, and a few weird things I ran into.

Table of Contents
  • What Is Universal Control?
  • System Requirements for Universal Control
  • How to Turn On Universal Control
    • On Mac
    • On iPad
  • How to Use Universal Control
    • Connect Your Devices
    • Arrange Your Display
    • Use Your Keyboard, Mouse, or Trackpad Between Devices
    • Disconnect Your Devices
  • Tips to Get the Most Out of Universal Control
  • Troubleshooting Universal Control Not Working
  • Universal Control vs. Sidecar: What's the Difference?
  • Final Thoughts

What Is Universal Control?

Universal Control basically turns your Mac into a remote control station for up to two other Apple devices nearby. For me, that’s usually my iPad and sometimes a second Mac. Here’s what I can do with it:

  • Move my cursor between screens like they’re one big display.
  • Type on my iPad using my Mac’s keyboard.
  • Drag files across devices like they’re butter.
  • Copy something on one, paste it on the other.

Each device still runs its own thing: macOS is still macOS, iPad is still iPadOS.

Heads-up: this isn’t the same as Sidecar. Universal Control doesn’t make your iPad a second display. It’s more like a remote-control setup. Universal Control works best when your iPad is properly configured. New users should first complete the basic setup by following this iPad setup guide.

System Requirements for Universal Control

This part tripped me up the first time. If it’s not working, it’s probably because one of these boxes isn’t checked:

  • macOS Monterey 12.4 or later
  • iPadOS 15.4 or later
  • Devices within 30 feet of each other
  • Same Apple ID on everything with two-factor authentication
  • Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and Handoff all on

Here’s what devices it works with:

How to Turn On Universal Control

Setup only takes a couple minutes, assuming your devices are already on the latest software.

On Mac

Here’s what I did on my Mac:

  1. Opened System Settings (or System Preferences if I was still on Monterey)
  2. Go to Displays > Advanced
  3. Enable Allow your pointer and keyboard to move between any nearby Mac or iPad.

Optionally, you can also turn on Automatically reconnect to any nearby Mac or iPad and Push through the edge of the display to connect a nearby Mac and iPad

On iPad

Then I had to flip the switch on my iPad:

  1. Open Settings > General > AirPlay & Continuity.
  2. Turn on Cursor and Keyboard (This option will be visible when Handoff is enabled).

How to Use Universal Control

Once it’s turned on, using it is super easy. Here’s how I usually get things going.

Connect Your Devices

I just line my devices up on my desk and push the Mac cursor toward the iPad. If it’s working, the pointer kind of melts onto the second screen.

  1. Position your devices close to each other.
  2. Move your cursor to the edge of your Mac screen toward the other device.
  3. Once you see the pointer appear on the second screen, push through to connect.

If it doesn’t connect: Open Displays > Add Display (+) and select your device under Link Keyboard and mouse to option.

Arrange Your Display

This part matters more than I thought. If you skip it, your cursor might jump in weird directions.

  1. Open Displays > Arrange on your Mac.
  2. Drag the device icons so they match their physical placement on your desk.
  3. Test moving the pointer between screens to confirm alignment.

Use Your Keyboard, Mouse, or Trackpad Between Devices

Once linked, you can:

  1. Move the cursor to the iPad—turns into a dot (until iPadOS 26 keeps it as a cursor)
  2. Type straight into iPad apps with your Mac keyboard
  3. Use gestures (see trackpad gestures for iPad) to scroll, access the Dock, or open Control Center.

Disconnect Your Devices

When I’m done, I usually just put the iPad to sleep. But you can also:

  1. Go to Displays > Add Display (+) > Unlink.
  2. To disconnect all devices: Press Control + Option + Command + Delete.

Tips to Get the Most Out of Universal Control

Some random tricks I’ve picked up:

  • Use Sidecar on one iPad and Universal Control on another. Yes, you can do both.
  • Keep secondary stuff like reference notes or timers on the iPad to stay focused.
  • Add gestures or shortcuts with BetterTouchTool if you’re picky like me.
  • Use the Display icon in the Mac’s top bar to check what’s connected.
  • If the connection’s flaky, turning off Personal Hotspot helped me.

Troubleshooting Universal Control Not Working

If it’s acting weird, first check your OS version and make sure Bluetooth and Wi-Fi are happy. VPNs can mess things up too. I had to disable mine once to get it working again.

Still stuck? There’s a whole Universal Control not working guide worth checking.

Universal Control vs. Sidecar: What’s the Difference?

These get lumped together, but they’re totally different tools.

  • Sidecar makes your iPad an extra Mac display. You get more screen space, and Apple Pencil works with macOS apps. It hides iPadOS while active.
  • Universal Control keeps each device doing its own thing, but you get to steer them all from one place. It’s more about controlling than extending. Great for file drops, typing everywhere, or using your Mac setup without juggling keyboards.

Final Thoughts

Once I got used to Universal Control, it felt like something that should’ve existed years ago. I don’t use it every day, but when I do, it’s a game-changer for juggling work across multiple Apple devices. Totally worth setting up if you’ve got the gear.

Got a favorite Universal Control tip? Drop it in the comments.

  • A complete guide to AirDrop on iPhone and iPad
  • How to Use FaceTime Handoff Across iPhone, Mac, iPad, and Apple TV

mainEntity.name: Does the Audio MIDI Setup method work with Beats headphones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, creating a multi-device audio output method works with compatible Beats headphones.

mainEntity.name: Will the audio quality be affected?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, using a Multi-Output Device on your Mac can affect audio quality slightly. However, for most casual use cases like watching movies, listening to music, or sharing podcasts, the difference in sound quality is usually not noticeable.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the microphone while sharing audio?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can't use the microphone from either device when you're using a Multi-Output Device on your Mac to connect two sets of AirPods, Beats, or other Bluetooth headphones.
